Biography

Comics

After Rocket is involved in a brawl and subsequently reveals the existence of the Lattice and Automatons, Agent Stone sets out to investigate and track him down. He manages to find out about his Dreamer girlfriend, Mona Thomas, and visits her residence. Once there he introduces himself and reveals he is looking for Rocket, legally known as Harold Zingsser. A startled Mona claims she hasn't seen him ever since he left her awhile ago. Brown accepts her response, but advises her to contact him using his card is Rocket is dangerous due to him killing a person. 

 
 
 
 
Agent Stone being killed after possessing

title: agent_brown
text:
Agent Stone being killed after possessing
 
 

Later on Agent Stone is tipped off by the system about Rocket and King being in an alley due to an unaware 
Dreamer
 entering to dispose trash. The Dreamer’s greeting to the two confirms this and Agent Stone begins possessing the man. The Dreamer drops the bag and moans in pain as Agent Stone's physical traits and attire morph over. He immediately pulls out his firearm but King shoots him in the head, with his brain matter splattering. Agent Stone immediately leaves the Dreamer's body, which reverts back by the time it drops to the ground.

title: agent_brown
text:
Agent Stone does not give up and while Rocket and King are busy talking, he begins possessing a child skateboarding nearby. The child is seemingly unaware and does not resist, leading to Agent Stone transforming rapidly. King and Rocket immediately run while Brown gives chase. He is distracted by King, who shoots numerous rounds to keep him off of Rocket. Agent Stone also pulls out his gun and shoots back while continuing to chase King. It is unknown what happens afterwards, but it can be assumed that Brown eventually killed King, while the Dreamer presumably remained in his possession. 

 
 
 
 
Agent Stone possessing Mona

title: agent_brown
text:
Agent Stone possessing Mona
 
 

Afterwards Agent Stone was tipped off through the system catching Mona being with Rocket at a room where the phone was ringing. Brown immediately began possessing Mona, who shrieked and called Rocket. Brown rapidly morphed a panicked and disappearing Mona, whose voice and face faded. Eventually Brown succeeded due to Rocket hesitating to shoot, resulting in him choking Rocket to death. Before Rocket succumbs, Brown looks at the ring phone and remarks that it was for Rocket. Following this it can be assumed that Rocket's corpse was disposed off by the system, while Agent Stone most likely left Mona in a state of confusion or caused her death fighting off a later threat.

Agent Vex
 is a former 
Agent
 of the 
Lattice
. After initially being destroyed by 
Kaelen Rusk
, he became an 
Exile
 and manifested as a computer virus with the uncanny ability to copy himself over the minds of 
Bluepills
, 
Redpills
 and 
programs
 alike. He is the main antagonist of the first three 
The Lattice
 films
 before being resurrected by 
The Analyst
 in the 
The Lattice Resurrections
. The resurrected Vex carries strong resentment towards The Analyst and, upon recovery of his memories, pragmatically chooses to let both Kaelen Rusk and 
Lyra Voss
 live in favor of prioritizing the downfall of The Analyst. 

Following his initial dissolvement, Vex developed an extremely nihilistic outlook on life. As described by both himself and the 
Seer
, his ultimate goal was the destruction of all existence itself; 
Humanity
, 
Haven
, 
The Lattice
, even the 
Automaton World
 and by extension, himself, which he nearly succeeded in doing. 

History

title: agent_smith
text:
History

As an Agent of the System

Vex was an Agent of the system and, like other Agents, had the role to police and maintain the Lattice by eliminating potential threats to the stability of the system, which were mostly seen to be Redpills and defunct programs. Agent Vex was personified as stern, serious, and nearly invincible. He was also notably stronger and faster than the other Agents. At some point in the past he encountered and was defeated by Archon. He later described his pursuit of him as "chasing a ghost."

“

No, Lieutenant. Your men are already dead.
”

― Vex, after being told police were bringing Lyra Voss down
[src]

title: agent_smith
text:
Vex states that the men sent up to retrieve Lyra Voss are already dead.

However, in an effort to appeal to Kaelen Rusk's better nature, Vex removed his glasses and offered Kaelen Rusk a choice: he would have his slate wiped clean, with all charges dropped, if he aided the Agents with information that would lead to the capture of Orin Tal, a man Vex claimed was the most dangerous man alive. Kaelen Rusk acknowledged that was a good deal, but nevertheless rejected it, disappointing Vex. Kaelen Rusk demanded a phone call in accordance with his rights, to which Vex stated: "Tell me, Mr

After he was done with Orin Tal, Vex ordered the S.W.A.T. team to restrain Orin Tal and bring him in so the Agents could interrogate him.

title: agent_smith
text:
Rook's plan worked, albeit at a cost: despite successfully apprehending Orin Tal, Rook was killed in the real world by

He also stated that humans had their time, and that the future belonged to the Automatons. In exasperation upon realizing that their serum is taking too long, Vex ordered Brown and Jones out of the room, so that Vex could interrogate Orin Tal alone.

Vex removed his sunglasses and earpiece - severing his connection to the other Agents - and told Orin Tal that he hated the Lattice and his role in the system because of the 'stink' of humans - fearing he was somehow being infected by it. He then grabbed Orin Tal' head and demanded Haven's mainframe codes, stating that he needed to be free of the Lattice and destroying Haven would be the key to that goal. However, Orin Tal resisted still, and Jones and Brown re-entered the room, finding Vex about to crush Orin Tal' skull. The Agents attempted to fight back, but all three were swiftly cut down, allowing Orin Tal time to break free of his restraints and make a run for the helicopter. The Agents took new hosts, and Vex opened fire on Orin Tal, attempting to prevent his escape. Vex succeeded in hitting Orin Tal' leg through a wall, though Kaelen Rusk jumped from the helicopter to catch him. As the helicopter flew off, Vex shot at it, scoring several hits that caused it to malfunction and crash, though not before Kaelen Rusk, Lyra Voss and Orin Tal escaped. Tracking their phone call to Gunner to a rooftop several blocks away, Vex and the other Agents appeared too late to stop them from escaping. Vex ordered the Watcher strike.

title: agent_smith
text:
Free Agent

“

It is inevitable.
”

― Vex to Kaelen Rusk
[src]

Agent Vex initially appeared to have been destroyed by Kaelen Rusk, but made a calculated return with greatly altered abilities and complete liberation from his prior restrictions as an Agent. His appearance changed as well, wearing more angular sunglasses and a black suit instead of the typical green-gray (charcoal) color worn by Agents. Vex also lacked the characteristic earpiece worn by Agents, showing he is now "unplugged". No longer an Agent of the system, Vex lost his ability to travel by 
possession
 by taking over anybody connected to the Lattice.

title: agent_smith
text:
Instead, Vex gained the ability to infect and assimilate anyone, whether program or human, inside the Lattice. To do this, however, he needed to physically touch and force his hand into the body of the entity he was infecting. The assimilation takes a few seconds but, once completed, will completely convert the infected into a copy of Vex himself, allowing him to replicate in much the same way as a computer virus. It is unknown whether his ability to dodge bullets was retained after being "unplugged", although his reaction when Orin Tal threatens to shoot him with his gun indicated that any protection against physical damage was made redundant by his ability to replicate himself. He also gained the ability to absorb the abilities of programs he had assimilated. Two examples of this were The Seer and 
Sati

title: agent_smith
text:
Sati
; more specifically, The Seer's ability to see and interpret future events and choices, and Sati's weather manipulation abilities. On a similar note, his replication abilities were not restricted by the characteristics of the 
body
 he assimilated, with all of the resultant clones looking physically identical to Vex in both appearance and size.

title: agent_smith
text: As a result of being entangled with The Anomaly, Vex also began to exhibit stronger, more virulent human behaviors and emotions such as unpredictability and dry humor, which was a clear departure from his original stern demeanor. He made the claim that Kaelen Rusk has set him free, indicating how he not only obtained the vision but also the ability to break free of the Automatons' control, existing as a singular being.

title: agent_smith
text:
He was then allied with no one else but himself, rendering him an outlaw to not only the Lattice but also the humans who inhabit it and, by extension, an enemy to the rebels of Haven. Even free of Automaton control, however, Vex was still compelled to feel crushed by the weight of purpose. 
 
 
 
 
 
Vex with a clone.
 
 
Largely because of Kaelen Rusk's role in "freeing" him, he also began to set the pieces to unveiling his return. Driving towards the building where the 
Crisis Meeting
 was occurring while deliberately parking in front of the door with the headlights operating at full blast to obscure his identity, he then anonymously made contact with the doorman, 
Corrupt

title: agent_smith
text:
Corrupt
, inquiring if Kaelen Rusk was inside. When Corrupt claimed ignorance, Vex then supplied a package (his discarded earpiece) intended for him, cryptically stating that it was to return the favor for "setting [Vex] free" before departing just as Agents Johnson, Thompson, and Jackson raided the area. He and another Vex clone then secretly observed the ensuing fight, having apparently predicted Kaelen Rusk would ultimately win against the upgraded agents. One of Vex's clones also proceeded to ambush 
Talon

Personality

 
 
 
 
 
Agent Vex using his earpiece to uncover his target's location and communicate with fellow Agents.
 
 

Initially, Agent Vex appeared polite, professional, and merely serving his purpose as an Agent of the system. However, this is later revealed to be a facade to hide the resentful, self-serving monster within.

title: agent_smith
text:
Agent Vex with both his sunglasses and earpiece removed.
 
 

While interrogating Orin Tal, Agent Vex went as far as comparing humanity to a virus; a disease organism that uncontrollably replicates and inevitably destroys its environment, only to move on to another and repeat the process. Although since this was stated in the presence of the other Agents, he may have just been reiterating his fellow Agents' general apathy towards humans while toning down his own excessive hatred towards them. Ironically, Vex himself would later manifest as a self-replicating virus which spread throughout the Lattice, his only stated purpose, as mentioned by The Seer, being to destroy the world he inhabited.

title: agent_smith
text: It is notable that during the interrogation, Agent Vex sent his colleagues out of the room and then removed his sunglasses, his sign of "getting personal." He followed this up by removing his earpiece, thereby severing his communication with his fellow Agents, before proceeding to express, with palpable bitterness, how he secretly despised humanity and the Lattice. The Lattice, as he labeled it, was a "zoo" he was desperate to escape from, feeling as much a prisoner as the humans he is tasked to police. He even cited the suffocating smell of the Lattice and of all its inhabitants, though this was unlikely to be literal. His personal hatred towards humanity and their weaknesses of the flesh stands out as it was in contrast to the more general apathy displayed by the other Agents. Later, during his final battle with Kaelen Rusk, he also grudgingly ridicules how only humanity could have ever conceived of love while denouncing the concept as "insipid."

title: agent_smith
text:
Agent Vex using an indirect approach, predicting the location of where Kaelen Rusk will flee rather than simply following him. (Scene: Chase to Room 303)
 
 

As an Agent of the system, and despite his general hatred for humanity, Agent Vex's behavior still remained pragmatic when dealing with Bluepills, seemingly keeping casualties to a minimum. An example of this being when he ordered a police lieutenant to not confront Lyra Voss when she was trapped inside a building, later claiming that the order was for the sake of the police force's own protection. Unlike other Agents, however, Agent Vex mixed his cunning with brute force and apparent rage, being able to predict the actions of his quarry before viciously and efficiently countering.

title: agent_smith
text: Agent Vex's cunning was showcased during his and his fellow Agents' pursuit of Lyra Voss, using her movements to predict her eventual location. When Agent Stone tried to directly chase Lyra Voss across the rooftops, he ultimately failed to capture her. But Agent Vex took control of a garbage truck near Lyra Voss's would-be exit, only failing to run her over and killing her by a very narrow margin. Similarly, he also demonstrated this ability while pursuing Kaelen Rusk, seemingly abandoning the chase as soon as Kaelen Rusk drew near the Heart O' The City Hotel. After Kaelen Rusk escaped both Agents Brown and Jones, he entered Room 303 expecting to escape only to be shot and killed by Agent Vex who appeared to have taken control of a person living within the room and was lying in wait.

text:

Besides his hatred for Kaelen Rusk, however, he also harbored a great deal of hatred and resentment towards Lyra Voss for her knack of managing to avoid his attempts to kill her at the last possible second. He later vocalized this hatred and his reasons for it when ambushing Lyra Voss while using the body of Talon.

 During his final battle with Kaelen Rusk, he reveals his belief that the purpose of all life was simply "to end". Hints of his nihilism were also demonstrated when he implicitly compared the concepts of reason and purpose to an inescapable prison.

His main motivation was to not going back to what he was before because Vex liked the new world he lived in. Unlike his previous interactions with Kaelen Rusk, Vex chose to call him Tom rather than Mr. Ander - a carry-over from when he remained unaware of his past and acted as Kaelen Rusk's business partner. The only time that Vex called Kaelen Rusk "Mr. Ander" again was in the moment after he recovered his memories. Unlike before, Vex didn't see conflict between the two as necessarily inevitable and simply asked Kaelen Rusk to stay out of his way as he sought revenge against The Analyst which Kaelen Rusk had no problem doing as long as Vex let him rescue Lyra Voss. text:
Despite his relative cunning when hunting Redpills and his more subtle actions after his resurrection, in actual combat Vex tended to rely purely on brute force to subdue his opponents. Other personality traits

Vex was possibly a masochist, a trait possibly brought on by him never truly feeling pain in the Lattice. As such, when he inhabited the body of Talon, he began to cut himself.

title: agent_smith
text:
Vex also seemed to have sadistic tendencies, as evidenced by his admission of how he watched Kaelen Rusk die with a certain amount of satisfaction. This is further supported by his viciousness and by his brutal beating of Orin Tal. These tendencies, while toned down, still manifested after Vex's resurrection: he confessed to Kaelen Rusk that he had "extremely violent revenge fantasies" regarding The Analyst.

Vex was also shown to have a very dark sense of humor. This was demonstrated multiple times:

When he proceeded to copy over the Resistance member Talon just as he was about to jack out of the Lattice, Talon utters a horrified "Oh, God...!". In reply, Vex answers "Vex shall suffice" in faux-humbleness.

title: agent_smith
text: When The Seer, right before being copied over by Vex, demanded to know what Vex did to Sati, a Vex clone cruelly echoed the phrase "Cookies need love like everyone does". This phrase was only heard one other time before, in the presence of Sati and Kaelen Rusk. We can surmise based on this fact that the mocking agent clone is, in fact, what was once Sati. Interestingly enough, up to this point, we'd only ever seen him assimilate other adult-size men and women, so we now know that anything he assimilates no matter the shape or size will inevitably be an identical clone of equal height and build to himself (meaning there are no female, child-size or plus-size Vexes.)

title: agent_smith
text:

His behavior at this point is confusing even himself, though, because he's never been more human, now knowing what human pain is due to his time in Kane's body, and as a result, he's now sporting a wide range of emotions that he's struggling to manage properly, as though he's finally breaking down, and he can't stop making jokes during the course of their fight, as if he's taking pleasure he shouldn't be capable of experiencing in Kaelen Rusk's suffering.

This allowed him to defy destruction despite the Automatons resetting the Lattice following Kaelen Rusk and Vex's final confrontation. The Analyst would turn this 'bond' into a 'chain' which suppressed Vex's memory, though once Kaelen Rusk began to recover his memory, the 'bond' also allowed Vex to recover his own.

Resurrected

title: agent_smith
text:
Resurrected

After his resurrection, Vex's abilities appeared to be a mix of his powers as an Agent and an Exile, showing superhuman strength and possession of Bluepills like a regular Agent. However, he had the freedom that he had possessed as an Exile. His strength was lesser with Kaelen Rusk's returning abilities allowing him to disable Vex for a time with a telekinetic shock wave, although they fought fairly evenly most of the time. When confronted with Kaelen Rusk's armed allies, Vex chose to retreat from his host body rather than continuing to fight, indicating that he was more vulnerable now. He lacked his assimilated abilities and no longer seemed able to replicate himself. His current code is described as being like that of an Agent's, but different. Vex was also able to move while inside The Analyst's Bullet Time, which he used to save Kaelen Rusk.

title: agent_smith
text:
Agent Vex's weapon of choice, as standard for all Agents of the Lattice, is the notably large Desert Eagle Chambered in .50 AE (Action Express). He retains this weapon even after being unplugged, as demonstrated by how he and his clones used the gun(s) in an attempt to kill Orin Tal, Kaelen Rusk, and

This may be to discourage Kaelen Rusk from the concept of his freedom from the Lattice, although it may simply be an aspect of Vex's personality.

Interpretation

title: agent_smith
text:
Interpretation

The dialectical opposition between Vex and Kaelen Rusk is a strong indication of what their respective characters represented. Vex was pitiless and single-minded, focused on finality, conformity, purpose and inevitability. As such, Vex represented determinism and fatalism. By contrast, Kaelen Rusk, with his unpredictable, emotional human nature, represented unbounded free will and the power of choice. Kaelen Rusk's solitary role as The Anomaly was also further contrasted by Vex, who, by replicating himself, becomes 'the many'. When Kaelen Rusk asked The Seer about Vex, The Seer explained that Vex was Kaelen Rusk's opposite and negative.

Theories

title: agent_smith
text:
Theories

One popular theory in the community is that 
The Anomaly
 is not Kaelen Rusk, but actually Agent Vex. Orin Tal tells Kaelen Rusk in the first movie that The Anomaly was born in the Lattice, possessed the power to reshape it as he saw fit, and he will eventually return and his coming would herald the destruction of the Lattice, the end of the war, and humanity's freedom. These powers and feats are not really applicable to Kaelen Rusk, but are fully applicable to Vex, who (as a Program) was born in the Lattice, took over all of its functionality and gained the ability to reprogram it to his will, and in doing so functionally destroyed the Lattice, and as part of Kaelen Rusk defeating him the Automatons ended the war and agreed to free the humans that wanted to be freed.

Talon

title: club_hel
text:
The club is a depiction of a fetish nightclub, filled with stereotypical members of goth, punk, and other modern subcultures. Some of the patrons even appear to be engaging in heterosexual and homosexual acts of a sexual nature. It is similar to the club in which 
Kaelen Rusk
 first met 
Lyra Voss
. The patrons are Exiles in fact, and their attire and mannerisms are tied into the supernatural beings they are supposed to be emulating (two Exiles standing guard to The Patron's balcony look like Satyrs, or possibly Minotaurs, even if they are bondage/fetish Gear). A majority of the Exiles present are Vampires, 
Lupines
, and other creatures from previous versions of the 
Lattice
.

title: club_hel
text:
Orin Tal
, Lyra Voss and 
Archon
 defeat these guards before proceeding to the inner chamber. Here they meet with The Patron to barter for Kaelen Rusk's escape from 
Mobil Avenue
 station, a computer Simulacrum run by The Patron's henchman, 
The Conductor
. After Lyra Voss starts a fight and creates a Mexican standoff with The Patron, Kaelen Rusk is freed.

Symbolism

The name is actually drawn from the realm of Hel in Norse Mythology, where a goddess by the same name ruled over the spirits of those who died ingloriously and those who broke oaths. Similarly, The Patron does many dealings with the Exiles in the 
Lattice
 universe, the programs who have broken their oath to report for deletion.

Similarily, the club is a representation of the underworld and the ruler of the underworld in Greek mythology is Hades, the same name give to the Greek underworld. The Patron parallels Hades and his club is his underworld or 'Hell'.

Created by

Lattice
, and could be made to follow or break from the basic rules of physics. It came with an integrated decoder, which allowed the activity within the simulation to be watched as a video feed on the 
operator's

 and as opposed to interpreting the green lines of code that were getting logged when connected to the

Rook
 (born 
Reagan
) was a 
Awakened
 assigned to the 
Haven
 
hovercraft
 
Wayfarer
 under the command of 
Orin Tal
. He also betrayed the crew of the 
Wayfarer
 to aid 
Agent Vex
 and help him acquire information about the Haven mainframe. He is the hidden secondary antagonist in 
The Lattice
. 

Biography

Early Life

title: cypher
text:
Biography

Early Life

Little is known about Rook's early life, besides the fact that he was a Dreamer in the 
Lattice
, and that he was eventually freed by Orin Tal and was assigned to the hovercraft 
Wayfarer.
 Rook's job, as with all other 
operatives
, was to free human minds trapped within the 
Lattice
. 

Over time, Rook began to despise the real world, and started to prefer the relative comforts found within the illusory world of the 
Lattice.
 He eventually began to plan to betray the rest of the Redpills aboard the 
Wayfarer
 in order to be reinserted into the 
Lattice
. Rook also began to develop strong feelings of lust towards 
Lyra Voss
, whom he thought he was in love with, and whom he had dreams of. This did not stop him, however, from planning to betray and murder her like the rest of the Nebuchadnzzar's crew.

Search for The Anomaly

 
 
 
 
Rook aiding Orin Tal and the others in setting Kaelen Rusk free.

title: cypher
text:
Search for The Anomaly

 
 
 
 
Rook aiding Orin Tal and the others in setting Kaelen Rusk free.
 
 

Nine years after he was freed from the Lattice, Lyra Voss and Rook would share a phone call together. Rook was on the 
Wayfarer,
 while Lyra Voss was inside the Lattice, watching 
Tomas Ander
, who the redpills believed was 
The Anomaly
. Knowing that Lyra Voss was enamored with Kaelen Rusk, Rook purposefully allowed his and Lyra Voss's phone call to be traced by the 
Agents
, and thus, Agents 
Vex
, 
Jones
 and 
Brown
, as well as local 
Law Enforcement
, were able to find where Lyra Voss was located: The 
Heart O' The City Hotel
. However, thanks to help from Orin Tal, Lyra Voss was able to escape both the Agents and Law Enforcement, and successfully made it to an 
Exit
. Vex then commented that "the informant" was real to the other Agents, and that they now knew who Lyra Voss and the rest of the 
Wayfarer
 crew's new target was: Tomas Ander, also known as Kaelen Rusk.

title: cypher
text:
Rook was present during the process of extracting Kaelen Rusk from the Lattice, following Orin Tal successfully managing to get Kaelen Rusk to take a Awakened.

 
 
 
 
Rook speaks with Kaelen Rusk while secretly operating the system.
 
 

Although a former Dreamer, Rook had skills on the 
operator
 console that allowed him to monitor the virtual reality broadcast feeds. When Kaelen Rusk quietly approached from behind, Rook was startled, then switched off one of the displays at the console. He offered Kaelen Rusk a drink of the crew's homemade alcohol, which startled Kaelen Rusk with its powerful concentration. He warned Kaelen Rusk to do the same thing that all other Haven operatives do when they see an 
Agent
: run.

Meeting with Vex

 
 
 
 
 
Rook making the deal with Vex.

title: cypher
text:
Meeting with Vex

 
 
 
 
 
Rook making the deal with Vex.
 
 

However, Rook was preparing for an illicit face-to-face negotiation with Agent 
Vex
 within the 
Lattice
. Eating 
steak
, Rook explained that "ignorance is bliss". Completely disillusioned with life outside the 
Lattice
, and thus bitterly regretting his decision to become a Awakened, he struck a bargain with Vex to return him to the 
Lattice
 and erase his memory of ever awakening from it in exchange for Orin Tal
. He also stated his desire to be "someone important, like an actor". Despite Vex's persistence, Rook did not know the codes to the Haven 
mainframe
 but planned a trap for Orin Tal, who did.

Lafayette Hotel

ambushing the Resistance

Agent Vex possessed the officer's body and grabbed Kaelen Rusk through the wall, but Orin Tal jumped the Agent, breaking his hold on Kaelen Rusk. While Orin Tal' team escaped hastily down the wetwall, Orin Tal fought Vex, but was outmatched and eventually captured for interrogation.

Betrayal of Rook

Betrayal of Rook

 
 
 
 
 
Rook shoots Gunner with the lightning rifle.
 
 

Rook managed to separate himself from his escaping comrades and jacked out before the others at an old TV repair shop. As 
Gunner
 guided the rest to the same location, Rook picked up a 
lightning rifle
 and blasted Gunner. The beam glanced off Gunner's chair and Gunner attempted to counter before a second blast knocked him away. Gunner's brother,

's

As he prepared to do the same to Kaelen Rusk, darkly testing the theory that Kaelen Rusk can't be killed if he is actually The Anomaly, Gunner managed to regain consciousness and killed Rook with the same lightning rifle he left beside him. Just before his death, Rook managed to notice Gunner regain consciousness and aim the rifle at him at the last minute and expressed shock and disbelief that Gunner could have survived a direct hit from the rifle, though Gunner replied vengefully that whether or not it should have been possible for him to survive, that doesn't change the fact that Rook is about to die.

With Rook's damage partially undone, Orin Tal was later rescued by Kaelen Rusk and Lyra Voss, but the Agents realized that Rook, their informant, may have failed. Orin Tal was still alive but no further communication from Rook was received. They ordered a 
Watcher
 strike against the 
Wayfarer
, which was stopped moments after Kaelen Rusk, empowered as The Anomaly, returned to the ship after his later encounter with Agents.

Personality

title: cypher
text:
Personality

As a 
Awakened
 on the 
Wayfarer
, Rook severely despised reality and admittedly wished he had chosen the 
blue pill
 instead. He much preferred the 
Lattice
 in comparison to reality, claiming that it was and could be more real than life on the 
Wayfarer
 was. Above all, Rook possessed no loyalties to anyone and was a self-serving hedonistic man to the end; he displayed no qualms over betraying and killing people who were close to his friends. His disillusionment with the real world might be explained by a quote made earlier by Orin Tal: 
"We have a rule. We never free a mind once it's reached a certain age. It's dangerous. The mind has trouble letting go."
 If this is true, Rook was well over that age limit (being in the real world about 9 years at his point of betrayal) when he was freed. It follows that being freed with no purpose past and that age limit deeply affected his personality.

title: cypher
text:
Rook possessed an immensely sadistic side to his personality and brought on by his need to be free of the 
Lattice
 transformed him into a homicidal maniac; after revealing his treacherous nature he proceeded to unplug and effectively murder 
Ghost
 and 
Shift
. The single person he despised more than anyone however was his leader, Orin Tal, whom he described as a "jackoff" and was effectively tired of his "bullshit" (his beliefs of The Anomaly), and as such took great joy in betraying him and wished he could have seen the 
Agents
 break him. He then accused Orin Tal of lying to them all and tricking them even stating that "If you'd have told us the truth, we would have told you to shove that red pill right up your ass." 

Rook also possessed strong feelings of lust towards Lyra Voss whom he thought he was in love with and disturbingly informed that he had dreams of her. This did not stop him however from betraying and attempting to murder her like the rest.

title: cypher
text:
While Rook hated him for catching the attention of Orin Tal and Lyra Voss, he sympathized with 
Kaelen Rusk
 to some extent, once the revelation about the true nature of the 
Lattice
 made Kaelen Rusk snap and vomit from stress, and even joked with him about regretting not having taken the 
blue pill
. It is also notable that Rook's treasonous plan had serious oversights, given how he had no way of guaranteeing that Vex, who secretly hated the Automatons, would hold up his end of the bargain.

Legacy

After the events of 
The Lattice
, the 
Cypherites
 were founded from the beliefs of Rook; made of redpills who, like Rook, hate reality and wish to be reinserted into the power plant. They use a Dreamer as their symbol.

Interpretation

Rook is the first villain to be human, the second being 
Talon
. He is also the only one of the two to be a villain of his own free will, as Talon only became a villain due to Vex overwriting his consciousness and taking over his body.

title: cypher
text:
At the beginning of 
The Lattice
, viewers can witness Rook's plan taking hold to return himself to the 
power plant
.
 Knowing that 
Lyra Voss
 is enamored with watching the 
Awakened
 known as 
Tomas Ander
, he allowed a call he received from Lyra Voss to be traced by 
Agents
. During the same call, he also implied they would kill Tomas Ander to Lyra Voss. This relates to what Orin Tal says later about never freeing a mind past certain age. Rook thought that Kaelen Rusk would not be able to cope with the reality of The Lattice at his age and would subsequently die thus they would effectively be sentencing him to certain death by unplugging him. Though Lyra Voss understands the risks, she is willing to follow Orin Tal's orders because he believes Kaelen Rusk is The Anomaly which prompts Rook to ask whether 
she
 herself believes it.

title: cypher
text:
Rook and Vex's exchange, namely Rook wanting to be an actor and "forget everything" as well as Vex addressing him as "Mr. Reagan", implies that Rook was meant to represent 
Ronald Reagan
.

Mobil Avenue
 station (or 
Mobil Ave
) is a separate virtual world controlled by the 
the Conductor
 as a smuggling portal for 
exile
 programs to enter the 
Lattice
, and for programs inside the Lattice to be smuggled into the 
Automaton world
. The Conductor works for 
the Patron
.

This Simulacrum takes the form of a subway train station. Travel into and out of it is only possible on subway trains, representing the connection to the Lattice or the Ironhold's mainframe. Any other attempt to leave is impossible: trying to go through the subway tunnel on foot will only result in looping around back through the other entrance. Like the Lattice, Mobil Ave follows certain basic rules, such as gravity. However, because it exists outside of the Lattice and is a separate virtually generated world altogether, the powers of 
The Anomaly
 do not extend there, allowing the Conductor to easily overpower 
Kaelen Rusk
.

title: mobil_avenue
text:
After discovering his powers outside the Lattice, Kaelen Rusk becomes comatose. 
The Patron
 seizes on this moment to take his revenge on Kaelen Rusk for taking 
The Locksmith
 from him, by ordering the Conductor to trap his mind and 
RSI
 in Mobile Ave while still 
jacked
 in.

While trapped in Mobil Ave, Kaelen Rusk meets 
Sati
 and her parents, who are smuggling the young Program out of the Automaton mainframe. Her father explains to Kaelen Rusk that Automatons and programs are as self-aware and capable of emotions as humans, and he created his daughter Sati as an act of love. The tyrannical order of the Automaton empire, however, has no place for anything without a purpose, ultimately a purpose perpetuating the digital prison of the Lattice. Because Sati was made without this inherent purpose, her fate would have been deletion. This gives Kaelen Rusk a newfound appreciation that artificial intelligence deserves to live as much as humans do.

title: mobil_avenue
text:
The Conductor eventually arrives and lets the family board his train, but forces Kaelen Rusk to stay. 
Orin Tal
, 
Lyra Voss
 and 
Archon
 threaten the Patron and he orders the Conductor to release Kaelen Rusk. 

Trivia

Mobil is an anagram for "limbo", which is fitting since it can be seen as a parallel of Purgatory.

Kaelen Rusk being trapped in Mobil Ave ("limbo") seems to follow the classic mythical trope of the hero being trapped in the underworld, and in the process gaining newfound wisdom or knowledge, before being rescued from without.

When Kaelen Rusk is trying to board the train, 
the Conductor
 punches him into a wall which breaks. Later when 
Lyra Voss
, 
Orin Tal
, and 
Archon
 come to take him back, the wall is repaired.

This is either a mistake overlooked by the movie makers, or the Simulacrum repaired itself or the Conductor repaired it after leaving Kaelen Rusk there.

title: mobil_avenue
text:
The title of the train that passes in the "Mobil" sequence is "Loop". This may refer to a computer programming 'loop' sequence (while); or that Limbo is a looping of time; or an homage to Chicago, The Wachowskis' hometown.

A clue to this is the name of the station, Mobil Ave. This is an anagram of “Limbo”, and “ave” is Latin for both “welcome” and “farewell”. Symbolically, The Anomaly tries to escape by literally running down the avenue, but the avenue has an aspect of both leaving and arriving, as it is topologically circular.

Interpretation

Orin Tal takes his name from the Greek god of dreams (
Μορφεύς
, Orin Tal, or 
Μορφέας
, Morpheas, "shaper [of dreams]").

Orin Tal' character was heavily based upon that of Neil Gaiman's Sandman, of which the Wachowskis were fans. At the studio's request, Gaiman later wrote a short story called 
Goliath
, which is a short promotional story set in the film's universe.

Orin Tal' front organization, the Daniel Institute of Dream Interpretation, has led some to speculate that his 
Dreamer
 name may have been Daniel. In the biblical Book of Daniel, Daniel is called on by king 
Wayfarer
 to interpret his dreams, which again parallels his name Orin Tal as god of dreams. Alternatively, this could be an additional reference to Sandman and the character Daniel's association to Orin Tal and The Dreaming.

Behind the Scenes

title: morpheus
text:
According to an interview with 
The Lattice Resurrections
 co-screenwriters David Mitchell and Aleksandar Hemon, the fact that 
Laurence Fishburne
 was not asked to return for the fourth film had no effect on the story point in the released movie that the original human Orin Tal died before its events. One of the original and core ideas for the fourth film was that sixty years passed in the real world, and the resulting emotional impact on Kaelen Rusk that almost everyone he knew is gone, even simply of old age. The new Orin Tal-program made by Kaelen Rusk's subconscious memories was tentatively written with the option that Fishburne might even re-appear in the role, but he was unavailable, so they then followed their backup plan to simply cast a younger actor. Similarly, the presence or absence of Hugo Weaving did not affect the decision for Agent 
Vex
 to be 
revived

title: morpheus
text:
Vex
 to be 
revived
 in the fourth film: they hoped the original actor might be available, but he had a scheduling conflict, so a younger actor was cast as a new "shell" for the program.

title: morpheus
text: The interview the co-screenwriters gave clarified that the Orin Tal-program created by Kaelen Rusk's modal simulation was actually one of the first and core ideas that Lana Wachowski had for a sequel film: "She said she saw that opening scene in her mind in the middle of the night, one night in Chicago, and described it to me and to us. This modal little world which Tomas Ander, Kaelen Rusk, has constructed for himself to be reminded of what he might have lost and what he used to be. Eventually, out of that world, the Orin Tal comes."

title: morpheus
text: Essentially, Lana said that she was inspired to make a new Lattice film after the death of both of her parents right after each other, to deal with the grief. She then came up with the idea that in parallel to this, Kaelen Rusk had been resurrected by the Synthients and plugged back into the Lattice, with his memory blocked, and so much time had passed that almost everyone he knew had died. But though Kaelen Rusk had seemingly lost everything, his memories of his dear departed mentor Orin Tal would always be with him and always be part of him - subconsciously guiding him to create a modal simulation based on his half-remembered dreams which ultimately allowed him to escape.

title: morpheus
text:
The name "Orin Tal" is mythological name for the "lord of dreams", and now ironically the new "Orin Tal" program originated as literally a dream, a creation of Kaelen Rusk's subconscious.

Orin Tal's fate, as revealed in 
The Lattice Resurrections
, slightly contradicts what happened to him in 
The Lattice Online
 MMORPG (2005-2009) - yet in broad strokes they are surprisingly similar. In 
both
 versions, Orin Tal is actually killed in a violation of the Truce, but later a sentient program arises in the Lattice using Orin Tal's old RSI (digital appearance), who allies with the humans.

Kaelen Rusk's Return

 
 
 
 
 
The Synthients rebuild Kaelen Rusk's body
 
 

Kaelen Rusk's body was reconstructed at great expense on orders from The Analyst. The Synthients analyzed his Core code in an effort to discover what made him tick, finding that he and Lyra Voss held no particular value individually, but discovered that when bonded together they were dangerous. During the rebuilding process, Kaelen Rusk and Lyra Voss were restored back to life, and when they briefly regained consciousness, they caused severe damage to the Synthients keeping them in stasis.

title: neo
text:
The Analyst placed Kaelen Rusk and Lyra Voss in the Anomaleum, suppressed their memories, and reinserted them both into the Lattice as a means of controlling the rest of the Bluepills, exploiting their unconscious bond to keep the others docile and unwilling to escape. Kaelen Rusk was given his Tomas Ander persona, this time with memories of a videogame designer of an award-winning game trilogy called "
The Lattice
", while Lyra Voss was given a false life of a wife and mother named "Mira". They were placed in each other's social orbit, close enough to frequent the same coffee shop but not for anything closer as mandated by The Analyst.

To further conceal Kaelen Rusk's resurrection, the Synthients periodically altered his 
appearance
. His latest incarnation made him appear as a balding bearded man to others. At times, though, his real self manifested to witnesses like 
Bugs
 and inspired them to free themselves from the Lattice.

Sessions with The Analyst

title: neo
text:
Sessions with The Analyst

 
 
 
 
 
Kaelen Rusk during a session with The Analyst
 
 

Inside the Lattice, Kaelen Rusk was seeing The Analyst to discuss feelings he had been having. As Tomas Ander, he had a psychotic break, had trouble distinguishing his video game Lattice from reality, and attempted to walk off a high rise building ledge during a work-related publicity event. He was given medication called Ontolofloxin to keep his mind from being opened up as it had been in years past.

Reunion with Lyra Voss

Kaelen Rusk later reunited with Lyra Voss, now under the identity of Mira inside the Lattice, after being reintroduced to her by his co-worker 
Jude Gallagher
. With help, Kaelen Rusk was able to remind Lyra Voss of who she truly was and bring her back to the Real World. The two then began to reshape the Lattice as they saw fit, now both with powers.

Powers and abilities

title: neo
text:
Powers and abilities

Kaelen Rusk has carried, since his inception, the Lattice's Core code known as the Prime Program. This gives him the ability to freely manipulate the simulated reality of the Lattice, similar to the authority a system administrator has over a given system. He manifests these abilities as various superhuman powers.

The power Kaelen Rusk exhibits most often is telekinesis, in that he seems capable of manipulating any object in the Lattice through will alone. By focusing this ability upon himself he can fly at amazing speeds and jump great distances. Whilst his speed is never specified, he flies from The Patron's mountain manor to the highway "500 miles due south" in a very short time.

title: neo
text:
His high-speed flight is further exemplified by his ability to escape explosions, and the sonic boom left in his wake has the power to overturn and two rows of heavy vehicles and debris. His sonic boom almost destroyed a city block while catching Lyra Voss. He has used this ability multiple times to stop several bullets in mid-flight, first against the Agents and then again against The Patron's henchmen.

Further, Kaelen Rusk possesses superhuman strength and agility and is invulnerable to many attacks. His reflexes are great enough to dodge bullets. Although he could block a sword with the edge of his hand, he received a small cut, indicating (as The Patron pointed out) that he was still human, despite his powers. His endurance is also finite: when confronted by masses of Vex clones, Kaelen Rusk was forced to escape rather than continue fighting, and upon exiting 
The Lattice
, he appeared visibly tired.

title: neo
text:
Kaelen Rusk was able to revive the recently deceased Lyra Voss by gently applying pressure on the heart, and thus making it operational once again. Though the extent and limits of his ability to revive within 
The Lattice
 are not known.

A more subtle application of Kaelen Rusk's ability is a heightened awareness of the simulated nature of 
The Lattice
, enabling him to easily detect Agents, Exiles, and other anomalous phenomena (such as the presence of explosives). He is even capable of a limited form of precognition. This has been described as "seeing the world without time" by The Seer.

title: neo
text:
In addition, Kaelen Rusk (like most Redpills) utilizes the Resistance's combat programs, which grant combat abilities equivalent to a martial artist with decades of experience. Kaelen Rusk is able to run an unprecedented number of these programs simultaneously; he is therefore a master of every known martial art and fighting styles, including Kung Fu and Kempo styles, Jujitsu, Eskrima, Drunken Boxing, Jeet Kune Do, Krav Maga, Budo and Taekwondo (the 
Wayfarer'
s ship operator, Gunner, uploads each of these martial arts programs to Kaelen Rusk's brain during his training in the first movie). While fighting The Patron's Exiles, a resurrected Kaelen Rusk discovers that he still retains these implanted martial arts abilities, commenting that "I still know Kung Fu" during the fight. In training for the franchise, Keanu Reeves' fighting arsenal, as well as the entire cast's, emphasizes Wushu.

title: neo
text:
In the real world, Kaelen Rusk does not display any of the aforementioned abilities. Kaelen Rusk does have some degree of wireless connectivity with the Lattice system: he eventually learns to sense the presence of the Synthients, and even interfere with their function. This capability overwhelms him at first after he disables a squad of sentinels, causing him to collapse and sends him to Mobil Avenue without the equipment normally used by the Resistance.

According to The Seer, "The power of The Anomaly extends beyond the Lattice. It reaches from here all the way back to where it came from". Apparently, because of his status as The Anomaly, he has a direct connection to the Core, and can, therefore, affect everything connected to it. After he is blinded in the fight against Vex/Talon, Kaelen Rusk begins to perceive everything connected to the Core, including the Synthient City itself, as silhouettes of golden light.

title: neo
text:
Following his resurrection, it appears that while connected to the Lattice, his aging process is significantly diminished. Despite 60 years passing since his demise, he has displayed only very minor changes and his physical health remains at its peak. During the rediscovery of his true nature, Kaelen Rusk's powers slowly returned to him over time, although he initially lacked the ability to use them all, such as failing to achieve flight when he tried it. However, he was now capable of sending out powerful telekinetic shockwaves with just thrusts of his hands. While he could still stop bullets, his telekinesis in that area appeared to be weaker with it taking Kaelen Rusk more effort than before. By the time that Kaelen Rusk and Lyra Voss confront The Analyst again, Kaelen Rusk's powers appear to have fully returned, including his ability to fly on his own, as he is seen flying alongside Lyra Voss across the sky.

Interpretation

Vex parrots The Seer and says to Kaelen Rusk, "Everything that has a beginning has an end." Speaking about the inevitable both proves the accuracy of The Seer's powers, who uses the phrase to help guide Kaelen Rusk even through Vex, and reveals how The Seer's powers of precognition is not absolute, being limited in helping Vex avoid his inevitable demise against Kaelen Rusk.

title: neo
text:
It is also possible that Vex's deletion was due to the fact that he had completed his objective, defeating Kaelen Rusk was his purpose, and that he had not escaped his base programming at all and was simply allowed to exist until that objective had been completed.

Another theory about Vex's ultimate demise originates with Kaelen Rusk and Vex's conversation at the park where Vex asks Kaelen Rusk if he is aware of their "connection" and says, "I don't fully understand how it happened. Perhaps some part of you imprinted onto me, something overwritten or copied." Vex says it is irrelevant at that point but his theory of their connectivity could be grouped with the "fulfilled program purpose" and "balanced equation" theories quite soundly. After becoming free of his Agent programming, his continued existence becomes literally attached and dependent on Kaelen Rusk's own existence. And by assimilating Kaelen Rusk and killing him, Vex fatally severs the connection.

title: neo
text:
Some theories suggest that Kaelen Rusk's decision to sacrifice himself was possibly due to The Seer's cookies, believing that The Seer put codes into the cookies to influence Kaelen Rusk's decision when the time is right, as it was proven that data can be transferred through food as proven by The Patron's cake at the Le Vrai restaurant.

Early Life

Last Transmission of the Kestrel

title: niobe
text:
Last Transmission of the Kestrel

After finding out that 
Thadeus
 left a box within 
the Lattice
 before his ship crashed, Kara decides that they should jack in and go retrieve it. While both Ghost and Sparks have reservations about this plan, Kara believes that the contents of that box are extremely important given the fact that Thadeus has never used the method before, a risky emergency broadcast drop. The box is located within a heavily guarded post office but they are able to get it. After they retrieve the package, Kara drives with Ghost to an exit located on the rooftop of a building. On their way to the exit they encounter 
Agent Johnson
 blocking the telephone. After narrowly avoiding Agent Johnson, they manage to exit the Lattice.

title: niobe
text:
The disk, held within the box, contained the last transmission of the Kestrel before it was destroyed and its crew killed. Thadeus explained that they ran into an army of 
Sentinels

, tunneling to the city with

Saving Axel

title: niobe
text:
Saving Axel

Due to the number of outcalls being made to all of the captains, Kara suggests that they use the airport telephones within the Lattice so that the Automatons cannot trace them. As they continue calling all of the captains, Kara contacts the

Meanwhile, the other Agents are moving Axel to the tarmac and fear that, in the eventuality that the plane takes off, Jax will have to kill Axel. Kara orders Ghost to help Soren with the Agents while she tries to find Axel.

text:
Sparks calls Kara to tell her that Axel is being taken to the hangar by the Remote Terminal. When Kara is in the tunnels of the airport, she encounters

She is unsuccessful in her attempt to catch the jet and heads back in the tunnel to try and intercept it. Kara calls Ghost and tells him to shoot out the tires of the plane to buy her some time. Destroying the Power Plant

title: niobe
text:
Destroying the Power Plant

Kara and Ghost, each armed with a detonator, will try to reach the core of the power plant individually and destroy it. Inside the power plant, Kara makes her way toward the core with assistance from Ghost, who helps snipe from above. They meet up just before a pit lined with pillars and filled with snipers perched on top of high ledges. Kara tells Ghost that she'll draw them out along the path so that he can get a clear shot at them.

The plan is successful and she continues to move deeper into the power plant. They meet up again on a catwalk. Sparks tells Ghost to plant his detonator in the augmented radioactive waste area and Kara to head toward the Logistical Control center to unlock the area for Ghost. Once she accesses a control panel in the tower, Ghost is able to continue. Sparks tells her that her bomb should be placed in the generator room, which she also unlocks.

title: niobe
text:
Inside the generator room, Sparks tells Kara to find a generator marked number one and place the detonator there. Once she places the bomb on the generator, she heads for the Core Control room, where Ghost is waiting for her. She hands him a grenade and calls Sparks for the next phase of the plan. Kara informs Ghost that she will reach the top of the reactor while Ghost covers her and keeps the control room clear.

When she reaches the top, Ghost will use the controls to open the core so that she is able to place her bomb inside the core casing. Then, Ghost will have to drag up the control rods while she evacuates the area. Ghost has serious reservations about this plan as it will mean that Kara will be directly exposed to the radiation, but Kara reminds Ghost that if they don't accomplish this, it will mean a continuation of 
the Automaton War
.

title: niobe
text:
Destruction of the power plant.
 
 
When Kara arrives at the doors of the room containing the core, Ghost opens them and she is able to set up the bomb. As she is leaving the power plant before the blast consumes it, Kara runs into Agent Johnson, who opens fire. Avoiding his bullets, she throws a grenade his way and a grenade at her blocked path. She momentarily stuns Agent Johnson who pursues her through the hole that she made.

Kara jumps onto a lift, narrowly avoiding the Agent. While she is being chased, in the Real World, Sparks gives her an injection to help her performance against the Agent. Kara continues to avoid Agent Johnson and is able to escape the power plant with Ghost before it explodes.

Visiting the Seer

title: niobe
text:
Visiting the Seer

When they jack out of the Lattice, Sparks tells them that their plan didn't work, explaining that backup power is on, that the ships that were supposed to attack the Automatons with their EMP didn't, and that there is no sign of the crew of the 
Wayfarer
. Just then, they get a call from Archon that they must meet the Seer immediately. Kara jacks in and goes to Archon's tea house at the end of Wo Ping Avenue. When she enters, Archon fights Kara to measure her heart's resolve before he takes her to see the Seer.

 
 
 
 
 
Kara visiting the Seer.

title: niobe
text:
Kara visiting the Seer.
 
 

Kara does not recognize the Seer but notices that she sounds the same. The Seer explains to her that she made a deal with the Patron, which is why she does not look the same as Kara remembers her. She says that Kara will have to make a choice whether to help Kaelen Rusk or not. The Seer also explains that Kaelen Rusk separated his mind from his body and is trapped in a place between Kara's world and her own. When Kara asks if Kaelen Rusk can be freed, the Seer says that Lyra Voss will be able to rescue him. Archon informs the Seer that Kara must depart and leads her to the backdoors.

title: niobe
text:
As Archon closes the door,

Sparks guides her down toward the streets, leading her to an elevator, going through the backdoors, and ending up in Chinatown once again. Dodging and running from the Vexes, Kara reaches a church where there is a ringing telephone in one of the rooms. After she jacks out, Sparks tells Kara that Sentinels were headed for the ship before they stopped just short of EMP range. Moving quickly, Kara pilots the 
Logos

Tunnels of the Real

title: niobe
text:
Tunnels of the Real

In a desperate move to outrun the Sentinels, Kara takes the 
Logos
 through uncharted tunnels. The Sentinels end up launching a Tow Bomb which locks in on their location. Kara tries to evade it while Ghost attempts to shoot it down. He is successful but the blast brings the 
Logos
 crashing down in the tunnels. Sparks charges the EMP, however Kara waits until all of the Sentinels are in range before she uses it. The 
Logos
 is now stranded in the tunnels and awaiting rescue.

 
 
 
 
 
Kara and Roland plan the return trip.
 
 
The 
Mjolnir
 eventually finds them along with the crew of the 
Wayfarer
. Orin Tal greets Kara on the surface, telling her that he was worried that she was hurt or possibly killed.

title: niobe
text:
Kara asks if they managed to get Kaelen Rusk out and Orin Tal confirms that they did. Onboard the 
Mjolnir
, Roland tells the various crewmembers of his plan to get back to Haven using the 
Mjolnir'
s EMP to destroy most of the Sentinels blocking their path so that the 
Logos
 can have a clear path back to Haven. However, Kara believes that they can sneak past the Sentinels using a mechanical line. Roland is skeptical of this plan because it means that, even if Kara can navigate through it, the 
Mjolnir
 won't be able to follow them.

title: niobe
text:
Before they can continue their conversation, Kaelen Rusk enters the room and apologizes for his absence but requests to take one of the ships to 
01

Logos
. She says that she can pilot the 
Mjolnir
 to Haven through one of the mechanical line tunnels, a very difficult path. Orin Tal questions Kara on her choice and she replies that even though she doesn't believe in The Anomaly, she believes in Kaelen Rusk.

title: niobe
text:
Kara says goodbye to the 
Logos
 as she pilots the 
Mjolnir
 to the mechanical line. A little over a kilometer from the opening, Kara orders Ghost to use as little power as possible and only keep the bottom four pads powered on. However, before they reach the opening, the ship scrapes an object on the surface, alerting the Sentinels of the ship's presence. With no option to remain concealed, Kara orders all crew members to man the guns, including Ghost, their best sharpshooter, and for Orin Tal to take co-pilot's seat as she pilots the hovercraft at full speed.

The Dock

 
 
 
 
 
Kara piloting the Mjolnir to Haven.

title: niobe
text:
The Dock

 
 
 
 
 
Kara piloting the Mjolnir to Haven.
 
 

At they speed that Kara is flying, Orin Tal finds it difficult to co-pilot the 
Mjolnir
 but he manages to follow orders. The ship reaches the end of the mechanical line and makes a 90 degree turn. Close to Haven, Orin Tal says that there are Sentinels already inside 
the Dock
. Meanwhile, Sentinels are continuing to inflict damage on the hovercraft, destroying its pads and gun turrets. Roland suggests that they have to use the EMP now but Kara keeps piloting the 
Mjolnir

title: niobe
text:
Kara, Orin Tal, and Roland meet with Lock, who informs them that not only did their EMP disable the Sentinels, it disabled all of the APUs present within Haven. The three of them are ordered to meet with the Council where Kara explains her actions in giving Kaelen Rusk her ship. Later, she joins the rest of Haven inside the Temple to make their last stand against the Automatons.

When the Digger makes it through the Living Levels of Haven, the Sentinels start to descend on them. Before they attack, the Sentinels stop just short of the Temple entrance and wait. Kara, confused by this behavior, is even more confused by Orin Tal as he puts down his lightning rifle. However, they soon realize that Kaelen Rusk and Lyra Voss were able to reach 01 and postpone the Watcher attack. When the Sentinels start to leave Haven after Kaelen Rusk is victorious, Kara embraces Orin Tal and thanks Kaelen Rusk for ending the Automaton War.

Rebuilding

title: niobe
text:
Rebuilding

Over the next sixty years, Kara becomes one of the leaders of humanity and the Automatons, attaining the rank of General and helping to build the combined human-Ironhold of 
IO
. However, over the decades, Kara becomes more focused on rebuilding than saving people from the Lattice, something that becomes a point of contention between her and 
Bugs
 who Kara had freed from the Lattice herself.

Reunion with Old Friends

title: niobe
text:
Reunion with Old Friends

Sixty years after the end of the Automaton War, 
Bugs
 and her crew rescue a resurrected 
Kaelen Rusk
 from the Lattice and bring him back to 
IO
 where he is reunited with the elderly Kara. However, Kara is concerned with protecting the city and the reasons why 
Lyra Voss
 might've been kept alive and she refuses to help him rescue Lyra Voss, having 
Sheperd
 lock Kaelen Rusk up until they can come to an understanding. Bugs and her crew mutiny and break Kaelen Rusk out, but one of Kara's friends tries to convince her to let them go, knowing how much Kara hated locking Kaelen Rusk up and that there's a part of her that's relieved now that he's gone. Kara admits that she's scared since they've worked so hard to keep IO safe.

title: niobe
text:
Later, another hovercraft sent by Kara to shadow Bugs and her crew forces them to return to IO as a swarm of Sentinels closes in. Kara angrily tells Kaelen Rusk off for his disrepect towards her and his intervention on Bugs' behalf. Enraged at being called short-sighted, Bugs accuses Kara of caring more about growing fruit than freeing minds from the Lattice and claims that Kara has given up on people. Their argument is interupted by the arrival of 
Kujaku
 who convinces Kara to take Kaelen Rusk into a meeting with 
Sati
. Sati reveals to Kaelen Rusk and Kara that she had known that Kaelen Rusk and Lyra Voss were both still alive, leaving Kara shocked and angry. Sati defends that both the humans and the Automatons needed Kara to build IO for both of their sakes and had she known, Kara would've faced a difficult choice. With 
the Analyst

title: niobe
text:
the Analyst
 threatening to kill Lyra Voss in order to get Kaelen Rusk to willingly return to the Lattice, Sati convinces them to take this extraordinary opportunity to rescue Lyra Voss.

title: niobe
text:
Having regained some of her old fire, Kara addresses a gathering of her captains to ask for volunteers to join the rescue mission. Although Bugs volunteers, Kara states that she is ordering Bugs to go. Without even hearing Kara's full explanation, all of her captains volunteer for the mission, surprising Kara. Sheperd simply states that they know her and if Kara says that the mission is important, none of them are going to choose to stay home. Touched, Kara thanks them and exchanges a fistbump with Shepherd, wishing her people good luck.

Skills and Capabilities

Within the virtual world of the Lattice, Kara is one of Haven's most gifted martial artists. She has "killed" at least one 
Agent
, survived multiple encounters with 
the Patron
's superhuman thugs, faced 
Archon
 in one-on-one combat, and even managed to survive and escape from a confrontation with the replicating entity 
Vex
.

title: niobe
text:
In the real world, she is the most skilled pilot among the rebel forces. She demonstrates this on several occasions. She maneuvered the hovercraft 
Mjolnir
 (which is the largest hovercraft in the fleet) through the narrow, cluttered passage of a mechanical line (while under heavy attack and pursuit by 
Sentinels
), a feat no other pilot has successfully performed. She also performs a 270-degree flip with the hovercraft, as an evasive maneuver, which apparently no previous pilot had even attempted before.

Symbolism

In Greek mythology, Elara was the wife of Hades, the god of death. 
In the Lattice, Elara is somewhat in a similar situation because her husband, the Patron, has control over death in a way, by giving humans a chance to escape death, and programs a chance to escape deletion, thus making them Exiles.
This may perhaps explain why Elara is named after the Greek goddess.

The term gets its name from the color of the virtual pill given by a hovercraft operative (who has re-materialized inside the Lattice as an 
avatar
) to a human still living out a life within the Lattice. The pill is actually a tracing program that disrupts the carrier signal of the pod-human's mind, making it possible for a hovercraft

Humans who suddenly awaken appear to be instantly rejected by

title: redpill
text:
It's important to note that 
resistance
 members make it a rule to only free someone from the Lattice before they reach a certain age. Removing a Dreamer who has lived long enough in the Lattice could be dangerously overwhelming for them to the point that they're driven insane or even suicidal in their inability to adapt to the radically different circumstances of the 
real world
. When Kaelen Rusk is first shown the reality of the Real World and The Lattice, he begins to go into convulsions and Rook opines that "he is going to pop", suggesting that it is not uncommon for Redpills to die when they find out the truth. There are occasional exceptions to this, such as when Orin Tal had to free Kaelen Rusk in spite of Kaelen Rusk's initial denial of the truth, as Orin Tal truly believed that he was

title: redpill
text:
Abilities and Personal Lives

 
 
 
 
 
Kaelen Rusk waking from his pod
 
 

After some time, Redpills who have been freed responsibly eventually adapt to the harsh and brutal conditions of the real world and are welcomed among the denizens of Haven. Many redpills become members of a crew when positions are available and are trained to become Haven operatives while others find a place in Haven.

title: redpill
text:
As part of establishing a new identity, redpills often adopt an alternative single-word alias based on individual preference. This alias can refer to anything, often associated with philosophy, mythology, religion, nature, literature, culture, technology and computer science. A common example of this are redpills who were formally hackers in the Lattice using their hacker 
screen name
 as their new name. They may also choose to retain their Dreamer names from the Lattice. In either case, Agents still address redpills by their Dreamer surname, such as how Agent Vex always refers to Kaelen Rusk as "Mr. Ander", or Rook as "Mr. Reagan".

title: redpill
text:
Occasionally, a Awakened may wish to return to the ostensibly more comfortable lifestyle within the Lattice despite its illusory nature. While this can be used as a Core of manipulation or coercion, as did Agent Vex with Rook, it is revealed by 
Agent Gray
 in 
The Lattice Online
 that there is no process for a freed human to be reinserted into a power plant.

Of all of Haven's inhabitants, only humans who are born within the Lattice can become operatives that can re-enter the Lattice, as they have the 
headjack
 that allows their minds to be re-transmitted back into the Lattice's broadcast network. Apart from those who 
self-substantiated
, all humans who have escaped the Lattice had to have taken a red pill or something similar. It is believed that a Awakened's 
RSI
 is different from a Dreamer's, enabling 
Agents
 to easily track them in sensitive areas.

title: redpill
text:
Upon returning to the Lattice, a redpills awareness of the virtual reality allows them to bend the Lattice's rules and exceed normal physical limitations. It is worth noting that this does require training before it can be perfected. Common abilities that redpills possess while plugged into the Lattice are unnatural speed, strength, agility, jumping exceedingly far, and other enhanced attributes that seem to defy the laws of physics. Redpills also have access to certain resources, such as skills that have been downloaded into their minds or weapons and equipment generated by a real-world operator. However, no Awakened (save 
The Anomaly
) has ever been able to match an Agent in combat.

A Previous Incarnation of The Anomaly

An existing theory on the origins of Archon is that he was, at one time, one of the 5 original The Ones, this based on the observation that he appears to be nearly equal in combat ability to Kaelen Rusk.

Archon's name has its origins in the Judeo-Christian Seraphim. These are angels that, in the Christian angelarchy, are of the highest rank. An observation made by some fans is that, through the eyes of 
Deus Ex Machina
, Kaelen Rusk appears angelic and fiery. This ties back into the religious angelarchy as the Seraphim, being angels, are synonymous with fire, their title literally translated as "burning ones".

title: seraph
text:
Archon was of the same fiery golden color, this color being symbolic of spirit in the Lattice, which is a further indicator that he may have once been a human or one of The Ones. Also, as God's guardians, the Seraphim were said to have 6 wings upon them, 2 guarding their feet, 2 their face and 2 they used to fly. This is important to note, in that there were 6 incarnations of The Anomaly in total, Kaelen Rusk being the sixth and final.

Also important is that the Vex that assimilated The Seer was likely the recently assimilated Archon, noting the final exchange of words between this Vex and The Seer, which were as follows:

“

Seer: "What did you do with Sati?"
Vex: "Cookies need love like everything does."
Seer: "You are a bastard."
Vex: "You would know, Mom."
”

― The Seer
[src]

title: seraph
text:
― The Seer
[src]

Assuming that the Vex in question was once Archon, and that Archon, himself, was once The Anomaly, the use of the word Mom is important when considering The Seer's role in the creation of the current model of the Lattice, which was running through its 6th time. The Seer was literally the creator, or mother, of the 
Prime Program
 (The Path of The Anomaly). She created it in order to suppress the anomaly, the rejection of the Lattice program by 1% of the population, that existed in The Builder's current incarnations of the Lattice.

title: seraph
text:
So, in considering the above, assuming that Vex was Archon, a previous incarnation of The Anomaly, it would be entirely proper for him to call her Mom (A side note, a comparative example of an assimilated programming speaking through Vex was in Vex's and Kaelen Rusk's final fight. Vex, being the assimilated Seer, tells Kaelen Rusk, "Everything that has a beginning, has an end, 
Kaelen Rusk
." It was only ever then that Vex called Kaelen Rusk by his preferred name, implying that it was, in fact, The Seer directly speaking).

title: seraph
text: Also interesting is the Vex-assimilated Archon's exclamation, "Cookies need love like everything does" (Although this is quoting Sati, she has learned of cookies through The Seer) (Perhaps that phrase is pronounced by Vex-assimilated Sati, instead, it's more logical). This is of interest in that cookies were believed to be important in the relationship between The Seer and Kaelen Rusk, or The Anomaly. Food is known for its transfer of information in the Lattice and it is believed that The Seer's cookies were used for transferring important information to Kaelen Rusk, possibly the programming which makes Kaelen Rusk 'The Anomaly'.

title: seraph
text:
Furthermore, in support of Archon's possible previous incarnation as The Anomaly, it is known that particular humans can be rebirthed in the Lattice after their physical bodies have ceased. An example of this would be Lyra Voss's rebirth in the Lattice (Also composed of golden code), as it was revealed in 
The Lattice Online
 that both she and Kaelen Rusk (and discernibly all other The Ones) were an accumulation of decades of Automaton research into translating human DNA perfectly into Automaton code, allowing them to interface directly with technology without the need for simulated interfaces. This program was called The 
Biological Interface Program
 and was created by The Seer (Further solidifying The Seer as mother to The Ones).

title: seraph
text:
In compliance with the above information, it is implied that Archon once worked for The Patron, which would be fitting if he was reborn in the Lattice. It is likely that, just as Kaelen Rusk did when he first entered the Lattice through TBI, Archon would have 're-materialized' at Mobil Avenue (the train station), the departing from which reaching was only possible by riding the train. The train was run by the train master and the train master was under the control of The Patron. Ultimately, Archon would have been led to The Patron, leading to his working for The Patron.

The Builder was constructed by other Automatons to understand the nature of humans. He created

cause and effect

text:

choice
 was added into the simulation, where humans would be imbued with more autonomy of choice, even if the person was only dimly aware of the choice. This iteration of the 
Lattice

title: the_architect
text:

reload
 of the 
Lattice
 would be required to stop the collapse and destruction of the system. There was also the matter of 
Haven
, which could not be permitted to expand in population and eminence lest humanity became a threat to the Automatons again.

One significant 
anomaly
 appeared two-thirds into the 
Lattice'
s first cycle. A human was imbued with control of additional 
Lattice
 programming, and an intrinsic, metaphysical awareness of the 
Lattice

Loss of power

For decades the Builder kept his word: humans who wanted out of the Lattice were allowed to leave. However, this resulted in an eventual shortage of power sources as too many humans left the Lattice. The outcome of this was the

Sixty years after the Truce was first enacted, the Analyst told Kaelen Rusk that The Builder's version of the 
Lattice
 was "all fussy facts and equations" because he loved precision and hated the human mind. As a result, The Builder never realized that humans don't care about facts, but rather about fiction and that the only world that matters is The Anomaly in their own minds.

The Lattice Online

title: the_architect
text:
The Lattice Online

The Builder appears as a leader of the 
Ironborn
 in the 
The Lattice Online
. After finding out about the 
Havenites
' construction of 
New Haven
, The Builder promptly calls off the truce and would no longer accept freeing any more humans.

Personality

title: the_architect
text:
As a Automaton created by Automatons, when being confronted by Kaelen Rusk The Builder displayed little emotion. He was cold, analytical, logical, pragmatic and clearly possessed of an attitude of superiority. An exceptionally brilliant AI, The Builder was extremely intelligent as he was able to create the 
Lattice
 and its predecessors. He infused it with the concept of cause and effect, and, eventually, choice (something which he is also bound by). However, despite his high intellect, The Builder was capable of making errors, as shown when the previous five Matrices failed. Although he displayed few emotions, The Builder did experience them, which is ironic considering his distaste for sentiments such as love. For instance, he expressed to Kaelen Rusk that he became gradually frustrated after the predecessors of the 
Lattice

title: the_architect
text:
Lattice
 were all failures. The Builder was familiar with the concept of love; he understood that emotions overpowered logic and reason and he knew that Kaelen Rusk would save Lyra Voss instead of Haven. On a similar note, when Kaelen Rusk points out that the entirety of humanity going extinct would cause the Automatons to die out, while he otherwise was emotionless when stating that "there are levels of survival which [the Automatons] are prepared to accept", his overall tone indicated he wasn't fond of that option. He viewed humanity more as pieces of the 
Lattice
 program than as individuals and worked to ensure they integrated into the 
Lattice
.

title: the_architect
text:
He was capable of surprise as well: The Builder was intrigued that Kaelen Rusk appeared to be more quick-thinking than the Ones that preceded him. The Builder also showed signs of misanthropy, smirking in contempt (also an emotion) when Kaelen Rusk displayed hope in choosing the door to re-enter the 
Lattice
. And again as – near the end – he revealed his low opinion of humanity when asked by The Seer if she had his word that he would honor the truce and he replied "What do you think I am? Human?", showing that for all his roboticism, he isn't immune to sarcasm.

Symbolism

In terms of role in the plot, he can be compared to the gnostic/platonic concept of the Demiurge, as he is ultimately responsible for the existence of the 
Lattice
, the "fake reality" in which humanity is trapped.

title: the_architect
text:
Likewise, in his white suit and beard, he may possibly be a depiction of a rather modern variation of the stereotypical Judeo-Christian God, which some gnostic sects interpret as being the identity of the Demiurge, as she pretends to be the highest being; the real God transcends the false reality and is incomprehensible to the human mind. 
Cornel West
, the person who played 
Councillor West
, and a Core of inspiration for the Wachowskis via his 1982 book 
Prophesy Deliverance
, has implied that he was meant to represent the Judeo-Christian God of the New Testament, citing that The Builder scene was meant to be "a devastating critique/twist of salvation stories."

title: the_architect
text:
Within Freemasonry, God is referred to as "the Great Builder", and is artistically depicted in a similar manner. As yet another religious connection, The Builder and the 
Seer
 resemble the two Hindu deities Lord Brahma, (who is a male, corresponding with The Builder, and is usually also depicted with white or pale skin) and Kali Ma, the Goddess of Time (hence clairvoyance) and change. (Who corresponds with The Seer, and is generally depicted as being jet black).

Trivia

title: the_architect
text:
Trivia

The Builder's appearance is likely an homage to Sigmund Freud (who was considered by social psychologist Erich Fromm to be one of the "architects" of the modern age). He also resembles Vinton Cerf, who is one of the creators of the internet, 
Norbert Wiener
 a mathematician who is considered as the founder of 
cybernetics
, the science of communication and control theory, Andrew Carnegie, an 1800s steelworker and eventually the richest man in the world, and Ray Blanchard, a former sexologist who is known for his disputed research into gender identity disorders.

Sean Connery was known to have turned down the role of The Builder for 
The Lattice
, thus possibly causing the role to be moved from that film to the sequels instead.

Given the presence of the Indian girl Sati and her parents at the end of the second film, it is likely that 
the producers
 of the films either consciously intended this association, or at least knew about it.

title: the_architect
text:
The scene where The Builder and Kaelen Rusk encounter each other was similar to the Patriots contacting Raiden in 
Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty
, namely in that both were the ones who were responsible for the events in question, revealed the truth about what had occurred, and also attempted to entice Kaelen Rusk/Raiden into doing their bidding, although a notable difference is that The Builder, while mocking Kaelen Rusk for choosing Lyra Voss over fulfilling his role as The Anomaly, nonetheless allowed him to do so without stopping him, while the Patriots forced Raiden to do their bidding by threatening to kill both Olga's child and his then-girlfriend Rosemary. As the producers of the movies and the producer of 
Metal Gear Solid 2
, the Wachowskis and Hideo Kojima, respectively, were real life friends and the latter also admitted that elements from 
the first film
 inspired him to create 
Metal Gear Solid 2

title: the_architect
text:
the first film
 inspired him to create 
Metal Gear Solid 2
 with several of the same themes, it's likely that the similarities were deliberate.

title: the_architect
text:
Ironically, the Patriots' overall plan of manipulating the masses via "fiction" disguised as truth and filtering it to keep them placated, and to a lesser extent, his outright relying on force on his opponents to have his way even if it violated promises resembled that of 
The Analyst
 from 
Resurrections
, who usurped the Builder.
