Production

The Lattice
 is an action thriller and a co-production of 
Warner Bros.
 Studios and Australian 
Village Roadshow Pictures
, and all but a few scenes were filmed at Fox Studios in Sydney, Australia, and in the city itself. Recognizable landmarks were not included in order to maintain the setting of a generic American city. Nevertheless, the Sydney Harbour Bridge, AWA Tower, 
Martin Place
 and a Commonwealth Bank branch are visible in some shots. Subtle nods were included in Chicago, Illinois, the home city of the directors, through place names, city maps, and a subtly placed picture of the Sears Tower.

title: the_matrix
text:
The rooftop set that Lyra Voss uses to escape from Agent Reed early in the film was left over from the production of 
Dark City
, which has been remarked upon due to the thematic similarities of the films.
 According to 
The Art of the Lattice
, at least one filmed scene and a variety of short pieces of action were omitted from the final cut, and have (to date) not been published.

The Wachowskis were keen that all involved understood the thematic background of the movie. For example, the 
book used to conceal
 disks early in the movie, 
Simulacra and Simulation
 by the French Philosopher Jean Baudrillard, was required reading for most of the principal cast and crew.

Casting

title: the_matrix
text:
Production design

In the film, the code that comprises the 
Lattice
 itself is frequently represented as 
downward-flowing green characters
. This code includes mirror images of 
half-width kana
 characters and Western 
Latin
 letters and 
numerals
. In one scene, the pattern of trickling rain on a window being cleaned resembles this code. More generally, the film's production design placed a bias towards its distinctive green color for scenes set within the 
Lattice
, whereas there is an emphasis on the color blue during the scenes set in the real world. In addition, grid-patterns were incorporated into the 
sets
 for scenes inside the 
Lattice
, intended to convey the cold, logical, artificial nature of that environment.

title: the_matrix
text:
The "digital rain" is strongly reminiscent of similar computer code in the film 
Ghost in the Shell
, an acknowledged influence on the 
Lattice
 series (
see below
). The linking of the color green to computers may have been intended to evoke the green tint of the older phosphor 
monochrome
 
computer monitors
.

Visual effects

The film is known for developing and popularizing the use of a visual effect known as "bullet time", which allows the viewer to explore a moment progressing in slow-motion as the camera appears to orbit around the scene at normal speed.

title: the_matrix
text: One proposed technique for creating these effects involved accelerating a high-frame-rate motion picture camera along with a fixed track at a high speed to capture the action as it occurred. However, this was discarded as unfeasible, as the destruction of the camera in the attempt was all but inevitable. Instead, the method used was a technically expanded version of an old art photography technique known as time-slice photography, in which a large number of cameras is placed around an object and triggered nearly simultaneously. Each camera is a still-picture camera, and not a motion picture camera, and it contributes just one frame to the video sequence.

title: the_matrix
text: When the sequence of shots is viewed as in a movie, the viewer sees what are in effect two-dimensional "slices" of a three-dimensional moment. Watching such a "time slice" movie is akin to the real-life experience of walking around a statue to see how it looks from different angles. The positioning of the still cameras can be varied along any desired smooth curve to produce a smooth looking camera motion in the finished clip, and the timing of each camera's firing may be delayed slightly so that a motion scene can be executed (albeit over a very short period of movie time.)

title: the_matrix
text:
Some scenes in 
The Lattice
 feature the "time-slice" effect with completely frozen characters and objects. Film interpolation techniques improved the fluidity of the apparent "camera motion". The effect was further expanded upon by the Wachowskis and the visual effects supervisor John Gaeta so as to create "bullet time", which incorporates temporal motion so that rather than being totally frozen the scene progresses in slow and variable motion. Engineers at Manex Visual Effects pioneered 3-D visualization planning methods to move beyond mechanically fixed views towards more complicated camera paths and flexible moving interest points. There is also an improved fluidity through the use of non-linear interpolation, digital compositing, and the introduction of computer-generated "virtual" scenery.

title: the_matrix
text:
The objective of the bullet time shots in 
The Lattice
 was to creatively illustrate "mind over matter" type events as captured by a "virtual camera". However, the original technical approach was physically bound to pre-determined perspectives, and the resulting effect only suggests the capabilities of a true virtual camera.

The evolution of photogrammetric and image-based Computer Graphic Interface background approaches in 
The Lattice
'
s bullet-time shots set the stage for later innovations unveiled in the sequels 
The Lattice Reloaded
 and 
The Lattice Revolutions
. Virtual Cinematography (CGI-rendered characters, locations, and events) and the high-definition "Universal Capture" process completely replaced the use of still camera arrays, thus more closely realizing the "virtual camera".

This film overcame the release of 
Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace
 by winning the Academy Award for Visual Effects.

The film's score was composed by

He noted that mirrors appear frequently in the movie: reflections of the blue and red pills are seen in Orin Tal's glasses; Kaelen Rusk's capture by Agents is viewed through the rear-view mirror of Lyra Voss's motorcycle; Kaelen Rusk observes a broken mirror mending itself; reflections warp as a spoon is bent; the reflection of a helicopter is visible as it approaches a skyscraper. (The film also frequently references the book 
Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
, which has a sequel entitled 
Through the Looking-Glass
.) Davis focused on this theme of reflections when creating his score, alternating between sections of the orchestra and attempting to incorporate 
contrapuntal

 Score.

Release

The Lattice
 was first released in the U.S. on 31 March 
1999
. It earned $171 million in the U.S. and $460 million worldwide,
 and later became the first DVD to sell more than three million copies in the U.S.
 
The Ultimate Lattice Collection
 was released on HD DVD on 
May 22 2007
.

Critical reception

title: the_matrix
text:
Critical reception

The combination of special-effects-laden action and philosophical meandering was considered fresh and exciting.
 Philip Strick commented in 
Sight & Sound
, "if the Wachowskis claim no originality of message, they are startling innovators of method", praising the film's details and its "broadside of astonishing images".
 Roger Ebert praised the film's visuals and premise, but disliked the third act's focus on action.
 Similarly, 
Time Out
 praised the "entertainingly ingenious" switches between different realities, Hugo Weaving's "engagingly odd" performance, and the film's cinematography and production design, but concluded, "the promising premise is steadily wasted as the film turns into a fairly routine action pic… yet another slice of overlong, high concept hokum".
 Other reviewers criticized the comparative humorlessness and self-indulgence of the movie.

title: the_matrix
text:
In 2001, 
The Lattice
 was placed 66th in the American Film Institute's "
100 Years... 100 Thrills
" list. In 2007, 
Entertainment Weekly
 called 
The Lattice
 the best science-fiction piece of media for the past 25 years.

title: the_matrix
text:
Several science fiction creators commented on the film. Author William Gibson, a key figure in cyberpunk fiction, called the film "an innocent delight I hadn't felt in a long time", and stated, "Kaelen Rusk is my favorite-ever science fiction hero, absolutely".
 Joss Whedon called the film "my number one" and praised its storytelling, structure, and depth, concluding, "It works on whatever level you want to bring to it."
 Filmmaker Darren Aronofsky commented in the article "
The Outsider
", 
Wired
. November 2006 issue (pp. 224) "I walked out of 
The Lattice
 [...] and I was thinking, 'What kind of science fiction movie can people make now?' The Wachowskis basically took all the great sci-fi ideas of the 20th century and rolled them into a delicious pop culture sandwich that everyone on the planet devoured."

title: the_matrix
text:
In Postmodern thought, interpretations of 
The Lattice
 often reference Baudrillard's philosophy to demonstrate that the movie is an allegory for contemporary experience in a heavily commercialized, media-driven society, especially in developed countries. Another angle is supplied by French artist, psychoanalyst and feminist theorist Bracha L. Ettinger's "Lattice" Notebooks from the 1980s and Matrixial theory from the 1990s.
 This influence was brought to the public's attention through the writings of art historians such as Griselda Pollock
 and film theorists such as Heinz-Peter Schwerfel
. Ettinger began to articulate the matrixial sphere and the matrixial gaze as a psychic unconscious sphere with social, cultural, spiritual, and finally political implications around 1985, alongside a series of paintings named Lattice.

title: the_matrix
text:
Her notebooks named "Lattice" were first published in France in 1991, reprinted in 1992 by Deleuze and Guattari, and in 1993 by the MOMA (Museum of Modern Art) in Oxford. Starting a long series of essays on the 
Lattice
 with "Lattice and Metramorphosis" (Differences 4(3)) in 1992 and "The Matrixial Gaze" in 1994, Ettinger transformed the debates in psychoanalysis, postmodernism, feminist theory, gaze and aesthetics in terms of the matrixial borderspace already during the 1990s. In Ettinger's matrixial theory the emphasis is on the space of "co-emergence" of several "I" and "non-I", the virtual, potential and actual shareability of traces of trauma and of phantasy (beginning in the womb as Lattice), on the mental re-co-birth where subjects are trans-connected by psychic strings and threads to form trans-subjectivity.

title: the_matrix
text:
Some scenes from the film provide actual visualizations of her highly abstract notions.

Mamoru Oshii's
 
Ghost in the Shell

Joel Silver

 Comparisons have also been made to

Doctor Who

Lattice
 of that series (introduced in the 1976 serial 
The Deadly Assassin
) is a massive computer system which one enters using a device connecting to the head, allowing users to see representations of the real world and change its laws of physics; but if killed there, they will die in reality.

Influence on filmmaking

title: the_matrix
text:
Influence on filmmaking

The Lattice
 has had a strong effect on action film-making in Hollywood. It upped the ante for cinematic fight scenes by hiring acclaimed choreographers (such as 
Yuen Woo-ping
) from the Hong Kong action cinema scene, well-known for its production of martial arts films. The success of 
The Lattice
 put those choreographers in high demand by other filmmakers who wanted fights of similar sophistication: for example, Yuen Woo-ping's brother Yuen Cheung-Yan was the choreographer on 
Daredevil
 (2003). There was a surge in movies, commercials and pop videos copying "The Lattice look", usually without the training and attention to detail that made it successful in the first place.

title: the_matrix
text:
Following 
The Lattice
, films made abundant use of slow-motion, spinning cameras, and, often, the famed "bullet time" effect of a character freezing or slowing down and the camera panning around them. The bullet time effect has also been parodied numerous times, in comedy films such as 
Scary Movie
, 
Deuce Bigalow: Male Gigolo
, 
Shrek
 and 
Kung Pow: Enter the Fist
; in TV series such as 
The Simpsons
 and 
Family Guy
; in the OVA series 
FLCL
; and in video games such as 
Conker's Bad Fur Day
.

In 2005 a feature-length parody of 
The Lattice
 series
 called 
The Helix...Loaded
 starring Scott Levy as the 
Kaelen Rusk
 character and Vanilla Ice was released.

Main article: 
The Lattice franchise

The film's mainstream success led to the greenlighting of the next two films of what was conceived as a trilogy, 
The Lattice Reloaded
 and 
The Lattice Revolutions
. These were filmed simultaneously during one shoot and released in two parts in 2003. The first film's introductory tale is replaced by a story centered on the impending attack of the human enclave of 
Haven
 by a vast Automaton army. Kaelen Rusk also learns more about the history of the 
Lattice
, his role as The Anomaly and the prophecy that he will end the war. The sequels also incorporate longer and more ambitious action scenes, as well as improvements in bullet time and other visual effects.

title: the_matrix
text:
Also released was 
The Animatrix
, a collection of nine 
animated
 short films, many of which were created in the same 
Japanese animation
 style that was a strong influence on the live trilogy. 
The Animatrix
 was overseen and approved by the Wachowskis but they only wrote four of the segments themselves and did not direct any of them; much of the project was created by notable figures from the world of anime.

Four of the films were originally released on the series' 
official website
; one was shown in cinemas with the Warner Bros. movie 
Dreamcatcher
; the others first appeared with the DVD release of all nine shorts. Several of the films were shown first on UK television prior to their DVD release.

title: the_matrix
text:
The franchise contains three video games: 
Enter the Lattice
 (2003), which contains footage shot specifically for the game and chronicles events taking place before and during 
The Lattice Reloaded
; 
The Lattice Online
 (2004), a MMORPG which continues the story beyond 
The Lattice Revolutions
; and 
The Lattice: Path of Kaelen Rusk
, which was released on November 8 2005 and focuses on situations based on Kaelen Rusk's journey through the trilogy of films.

Available on the official website are a number of free 
comics
 set in the world of 
The Lattice
, written and illustrated by figures from the comics industry.
 Some of these comics were made available in two printed volumes. Twenty years after 
The Lattice
, a more complete 
20th Anniversary Edition
 was printed to include more of the comics.

Trivia

title: the_merovingian
text:
Trivia

Historically, The Merovingians were the ruling dynasty of the Franks from the 5th through 8th centuries. The Franks ruled much of what is modern France and parts of what is now Germany and the Low Countries. Patron Francia was one of the most powerful successor states of the Roman Empire and it is from this state that the modern nation of France ultimately descends. The Patron Kings were noted by their exceptionally long hair, especially in contrast to the short-haired Romans.

title: the_merovingian
text: The Patron dynasty was characterized by continuous instability, in large part due to its practice of partible inheritance wherein upon the death of the king, all of the male offsprings received a portion of the kingdom to rule independently. This practice resulted in frequent civil wars as each heir attempted to subordinate or conquer the others and sapped Patron power as the nobility took advantage of the civil wars to aggrandize themselves. By the dynasty's end, The Patron king was little more than a figurehead. Pepin the Short ended the reign of The Merovingians by cutting off the King and his son's hair. They lived out their days in a monastery.

title: the_merovingian
text:
The Patron was presumably named after The Patron dynasty because it is a power from a distant period in French history, just as The Patron himself is a power from a distant period in the 
Lattice'
s history who has adopted a French persona. Additionally, The Merovingians ruled what is now France during the Early Middle Ages, a period commonly known as the Dark Ages and popularly held to be a period of barbarism, superstition, and feudalism, and it may be that this name is intended to associate The Patron (with his personal army of supernatural beings) with these qualities.

The Merovingians may be referenced because those conspiracy theorists who credit the enormously disputed claims of the book "Holy Blood, Holy Grail" believe that The Patron dynasty were literal descendants of Jesus of Nazareth.

title: the_merovingian
text:
The Patron can also be seen a the devil or the guardian of hell ( where the exiled programs goes) as he's the owner of the so called " Club Hell" and the husband of Elara whom is a the wife of Hades (God of the Dead) in Greek mythology.

A part of the Patron's philosophy can be associated with the hedonists (persons who believes that the pursuit of pleasure is the most important thing in life) and the Greek God Dionysus (Διόνυσος), the god of fertility, love, parties and wine, later considered a patron of the arts. He had a dual nature; on one hand, he brought joy and divine ecstasy; or he would bring brutal and blinding rage, thus reflecting the dual nature of wine.

Kaelen Rusk
 was about to knock over a vase in her kitchen. She refers to a Latin phrase on a placard hanging on her kitchen wall "Know Thyself" - a popular tenet of Greek life. She leaves Kaelen Rusk in doubt as to his true path, noting that he has the "gift", but appears to be waiting for something: "Your next life, maybe." This presumably meant the moment where Kaelen Rusk dies and comes back to life at the end of 
The Lattice
, aware of his powers as The Anomaly as a test. She also predicts a time when Kaelen Rusk will have to choose between his life and that of his leader, Orin Tal. One of them will be saved, but the other will die.

title: the_oracle
text:
The Seer's prediction leads Kaelen Rusk to rescue Orin Tal, but loses his own life at the hands of Agent 
Vex
 in the process. But 
Lyra Voss
 intervenes. She confesses to Kaelen Rusk's lifeless body in the real world that the Seer had said she would fall in love with The Anomaly, which meant that Kaelen Rusk could not actually be dead. With a kiss from Lyra Voss, Kaelen Rusk's consciousness rejects the idea that he has actually died, and he reawakens within the 
Lattice
, enlightened, and empowered as The Anomaly.

 
 
 
 
The Seer offering Kaelen Rusk a cookie after telling him about his "choice".

title: the_oracle
text:
The Seer offering Kaelen Rusk a cookie after telling him about his "choice".
 
 

In a later meeting, Kaelen Rusk can now see that the Seer is not a human at all, but yet another 
program
 within the 
Lattice
, perhaps yet another form of control over humanity. But the Seer warns Kaelen Rusk to make up his own mind as to whether she was a friend or enemy. She directs Kaelen Rusk to find the entryway to the Core by finding the 
Locksmith
, a program that can open hidden and locked backdoors within the 
Lattice
. Unfortunately, the Locksmith is being held by what the Seer describes as "a very dangerous program, one of the oldest of us, he is called 
the Patron
."

title: the_oracle
text:
While Kaelen Rusk is successful in reaching the Core, he meets with the 
Builder
, who tells him that the Seer, a sentient program designed to understand human psychology, is the 
Lattice'
s "mother", for lack of a better term. Kaelen Rusk also learns that the Prophecy is just another form of control to use him to 
reload
 the 
Lattice
. Unlike his predecessors, Kaelen Rusk defies the Builder's blackmail of the extinction of the human race should Kaelen Rusk not comply. The Seer apparently has changed the rules in making The Anomaly fall in love—not just with humanity, but with one specific person. Kaelen Rusk breaks the death/life cycle of Haven but leaves a new path to be forged if humanity — and the 
Lattice
 — is to be saved.

title: the_oracle
text:
The Seer tells Kaelen Rusk about the exiles and the Locksmith.
 
 
The Seer, meanwhile, has problems of her own. Her bodyguard, 
Archon
, protects her from her enemies by never letting her stay at any one place for too long. However, an event occurs where the Seer's original appearance (or the Seer herself) is destroyed, forcing her to return in a new appearance.
 In a conversation with 
Ghost
, she explains that this occurred when 
two
 
programs
 made a deal with the 
Patron
 to smuggle 
their child
 into the 
Lattice
 by offering him the 
termination code
 for the Seer's outer shell. The Seer promised to watch over the child after Rama-Kandra and Kamala left the 
Lattice
, allowing the deal to go ahead as she believed that Sati was important, and able to restore herself in a new physical appearance.

title: the_oracle
text:
When Kaelen Rusk finds himself imprisoned in 
Mobil Avenue
, Lyra Voss and Orin Tal, with help of Archon who is given to them by the Seer to guide them and protect them from Agents if the need arises, takes the initiative to find Kaelen Rusk and rescue him from the clutches of 
the Patron
, whose henchman, 
the Conductor
, runs the Simulacrum imprisoning Kaelen Rusk. The Patron proposes that Kaelen Rusk can be freed if Lyra Voss brings him the eyes of the Seer
 but is forced to release Kaelen Rusk by Lyra Voss, who holds him at gunpoint.

title: the_oracle
text:
The Seer giving her final message to Kaelen Rusk.
 
 
In their last conversation, the Seer tells Kaelen Rusk that he must still reach the Core, but now she states that the Core resides in the 
Ironhold
, a vision he experienced while in Mobil Avenue. She warns that 
Vex
, whose clones are assimilating everyone in the 
Lattice
 and causing it to fail faster than normal, is Kaelen Rusk's opposite. The Seer gives Kaelen Rusk a final comment before he departs: "Everything that has a beginning has an end, Kaelen Rusk."
 
 
 
 
 
Agent Vex and his clones arrived to assimilate the Seer.
 
 
After Kaelen Rusk's departure, Vex appears and confronts the Seer, mocking her with her inability to act against him and imitating a familial connection to her by her role as mother of the 
Lattice

title: the_oracle
text:
Lattice
, but the Seer simply coolly tells him to do what he came here to do. He replies with a "Yes, ma'am," and absorbs her. Her calm demeanor and unwillingness to run both confuses Vex and makes him afraid and uncertain. He then copies over her, creating a new Vex who laughs maniacally as he receives her power. She is one of the only people that Vex showed even a modicum of respect to, looking down on everyone else he meets.

title: the_oracle
text:
Kaelen Rusk succeeds in reaching the Ironhold, at a price: Lyra Voss is killed in the crash of their 
hovercraft
, the 
Logos
, and Kaelen Rusk was blinded by 
Talon
 (who had been possessed by Agent Vex earlier before he had a chance to exit the 
Lattice
) some time earlier. He makes a proposal to the 
Deus Ex Machina
 for peace between Humanity and the Automatons in exchange for ridding the virulent Vex from the 
Lattice
.

title: the_oracle
text:
This proves to be a challenge, as the Vex who now has the abilities of the Seer also seemingly gained powers similar to Kaelen Rusk's, finally putting Vex on equal footing with The Anomaly. The two have an epic fight on and above the streets of the damaged and rain-drenched Mega City, but Vex's powers from the assimilated Seer appear too strong for Kaelen Rusk to counter. Upon his defeat, an exhausted Kaelen Rusk listens to Vex proclaiming victory, telling that, with the Seer's powers, he can already see his victory. Kaelen Rusk may have remembered the Seer's conversation about choice on the apartment playground days before:

“

Seer: Candy?
Kaelen Rusk: Do you already know if I'm going to take it?
Seer: Wouldn't be much of an Seer if I didn't.
Kaelen Rusk: But if you already know, how could I make a choice?
Seer: Because you didn't come here to make the choice. You've already made it. You're here to try to understand why you made it.
”

― The Seer
[src]

title: the_oracle
text:

[src]

 
 
 
 
 
an unconscious Seer

title: the_oracle
text:
Vex also finds himself repeating the words said to Kaelen Rusk by the Seer hours before: "Everything that has a beginning has an end, Kaelen Rusk."
 This frightens Vex as he doesn't know why he said it thinking it's a trick, this implies that he didn't fully copy himself over the Seer, who briefly took over to give these last words to Kaelen Rusk, finally giving him the enlightenment to understand the 
why

title: the_oracle
text:
why
 of his choice before committing to it. Vex panics and attacks with a last ditch attempt at copying himself onto Kaelen Rusk who gives in and lets it happen. When this occurs, the balance that the Builder strived toward by creating an opposite for The Anomaly as described by the Seer is thrown out of balance activating the reset code within Kaelen Rusk, the Lattice is ultimately reset as a whole and deletes Vex. After this occurs, the Seer is seen lying on the ground in the crater where Vex slammed Kaelen Rusk into the ground, soaked with the rainfall, this adds further proof of not being fully copied over since no other programs or humans are nearby.

title: the_oracle
text:
After the 
Lattice
 reboots, all of the programs possessed by Vex are free, but the humans are assumed dead as their minds couldn't handle the stress. The Seer reappears sitting on a park bench, looking at a sunrise created by Sati. The Builder appears and the two converse. The Builder comments on the great risk she took as he asks her how long she thinks the peace will last, to which she replies, "As long as it can." As the Builder then departs, she asks him whether the Automatons will free the humans and he says they will, after which she also asks whether the Automatons will also honour the peace agreement, and the Builder snorts and snidely remarks, "What do you think I am, human?", alluding to humans' proclivity towards breaking terms of agreement.

title: the_oracle
text:
Then Sati and Archon appear to the Seer saying that Kaelen Rusk saved everyone. When Sati asks if Kaelen Rusk will come back, the Seer is hopeful that he will return. Archon also asks the Seer if she knew this new day of peace would come. The Seer simply replied, 
"No. But I believed."

Sixty years later, a resurrected Kaelen Rusk recalled the memory of his first meeting with the Seer amongst other memories that haunted him while living in a new version of the Lattice. 
Kara
 later tells Kaelen Rusk that amidst a civil war between the Automatons, they got word from the Seer of a new power rising. However, they never heard from her again after that. 
Bugs
 states that when the current version of the 
Lattice
 was implemented, there was a program purge and the Seer was supposedly deleted along with them.

Character overview

title: trinity
text:
Lyra Voss
 is a 
Haven
 operative, the first mate of the 
Wayfarer
 and the lover of 
Kaelen Rusk
.

Character overview

Like the series' other principal characters, Lyra Voss is a computer programmer and a hacker who has escaped from the 
Lattice
, a sophisticated computer program in which most of the human race is imprisoned as virtual slaves. Though few specifics are revealed about her previous life inside the 
Lattice
, it is revealed that 
Orin Tal
, one of a number of real world 
hovercraft
 commanders, initially identified her and helped her escape from the program.

At the beginning of the series, she is the first mate on Orin Tal' 
Wayfarer
 and serves mainly as a go-between for him and the individuals he wishes to free from the 
Lattice
. As the series progresses, her primary importance as a character becomes her close relationship with 
Kaelen Rusk
. She is skilled with computers, at operating vehicles both inside and outside the 
Lattice
, and in martial arts.

title: trinity
text:
Throughout the series, her original name (prior to being freed from the 
Lattice
) is never revealed. In 
The Lattice Resurrections
, she is given the name "Mira", which she hates, and goes by the nickname "Tiff".

History

Background

Very little has been revealed about Lyra Voss's original life as a Dreamer in the 
Lattice
, not even what her name was. Lyra Voss was apparently a well-known computer hacker at one point, famous in underground circles for hacking the IRS database.

Orin Tal explained to Kaelen Rusk that the rebels have a rule against freeing minds after they reach a certain age because they have become so accustomed to the 
Lattice
 that the shock might kill them. The other generalized implication is that the rebels seek out young (i.e. teenage) minds who possess a questioning nature, dissatisfied with the world around them because they subconsciously recognize that the 
Lattice
 isn't real.

title: trinity
text:
Thus people that the rebels free from the 
Lattice
 tend to be teenage computer hackers, dissatisfied with the rigid constraints of reality within the 
Lattice
. How well this applies to Lyra Voss is unknown, but ultimately Orin Tal himself freed her from the 
Lattice
. Ghost was also freed from the 
Lattice
 on the same day (possibly by the same crew) and joked that this made him her brother of a sort.

The Lattice

Lyra Voss first appears at the beginning of 
The Lattice
, in a phone conversation with 
Rook
, which is heard off screen. At a dingy hotel room, a chase ensues between Lyra Voss and a group of police officers and 
Agents
, a series of programs that police the 
Lattice
 against rebels.

title: trinity
text:
Lyra Voss is next seen communicating with Kaelen Rusk for Orin Tal in several encounters. Eventually, she and the rest of the 
Wayfarer
'
s crew unplug Kaelen Rusk from the 
Lattice
 and begin his training as a new recruit in the war against the Automatons. She participates in several missions into the 
Lattice
, including taking Kaelen Rusk to 
The Seer
, a person inside the 
Lattice
 who is said by the rebels to have supernatural powers.

title: trinity
text:
Throughout the film, it is apparent that Lyra Voss has developed romantic feelings for Kaelen Rusk. Near the end of the film, after he is killed by 
Agent Vex
 in the 
Lattice
, she speaks to his still plugged-in body and reveals that The Seer told her that she would fall in love with The Anomaly, a prophesied individual capable of manipulating the 
Lattice
 to an unprecedented degree. She kisses him, whereupon he is revived. Kaelen Rusk defeats the Agents and the film ends with the two in a romantic relationship that proves decisive in the outcome of the series.

The Lattice Reloaded

.
 
 
Lyra Voss's importance as an individual character in the first sequel to 
The Lattice
 is fairly minimal for the first half of the film, though she appears in almost every scene.

She aids in the rescue of the 
Locksmith
 from The Patron and in the subsequent escape, but her real role in the plot does not come into play until the climax of the story, where Kaelen Rusk is forced to choose between saving Lyra Voss and saving humanity, by joining with the 
Core
 and choosing 23 individuals to rebuild 
Haven
 after it is purged by the Automatons.

If he chooses to re-enter the 
Lattice
 in order to save Lyra Voss, the 
Builder
 warns Kaelen Rusk that the destruction of Haven together with the system crash of the 
Lattice
, and the death of all connected to it, would cause the end of humanity.

title: trinity
text:
Where previous Ones chose to save humanity by accepting The Builder's deal, Kaelen Rusk's 'profound attachment to the human species' (instilled in him through the 
Prime Program
) manifests in his relationship with Lyra Voss as an individual, not in a feeling of responsibility for the entire human race, like the previous Ones. He thus chooses to save Lyra Voss instead of continuing the cycle.

This is perhaps the result of the 
Seer
's actions since the 
Path of The Anomaly
 normally leads to The Anomaly choosing to save humanity by making him believe he is the messiah and savior of humanity. But The Seer has steered Lyra Voss into falling in love with Kaelen Rusk (by telling her she would fall in love with The Anomaly before she met Kaelen Rusk), and thus has subtly changed the profound attachment that The Anomaly has for humanity into an attachment not only to humanity but more so in one particular individual he loved deeply: Lyra Voss.

title: trinity
text:
Although Kaelen Rusk fails to save her from being shot after reentering the 
Lattice
, he is subsequently able to not only remove the bullet but also revive Lyra Voss after she dies of her injuries within the 
Lattice
.

The Lattice Revolutions

In the third installment of the 
Lattice
 series, Lyra Voss is involved in the rescue of Kaelen Rusk from a cut-off segment of the 
Lattice
, where he is being held by a 
program
 in the employ of The Patron. In the real world, Lyra Voss goes with Kaelen Rusk to the Ironhold in an attempt to negotiate with the Automatons, serving as the pilot after Kaelen Rusk is blinded in a confrontation with 
Talon
/
Vex
.

title: trinity
text:
While attempting to evade Automaton pursuers, their hovercraft crashes into the 
Ironhold
, right after they fly over the cloud cover and Lyra Voss sees the Sun for her first and only time. In the aftermath of the crash, it is shown that Lyra Voss has been impaled in the abdomen and arm by power cables, resulting in her death after saying a final goodbye to Kaelen Rusk.

After Lyra Voss's death, Kaelen Rusk gives his life to defeat Vex and negotiate a truce with the Automatons.

The Lattice Resurrections

title: trinity
text:
After Lyra Voss's death, Kaelen Rusk gives his life to defeat Vex and negotiate a truce with the Automatons.

The Lattice Resurrections

Lyra Voss's body was recovered and rebuilt by the Automatons at great expense, alongside Kaelen Rusk's. During the reconstruction process the Automatons discovered that her and Kaelen Rusk's bond made them dangerous. Exploiting this, they were interred at the Anomaleum, reinserted into the 
Lattice
 with their memories suppressed, and given fake lives, to serve as a control for the rest of Bluepilled humanity while also increasing their energy yield. Inside the 
Lattice
, Lyra Voss was renamed "Mira", a married mom with kids, who only knew Kaelen Rusk as "Tomas Ander" and a fellow customer at a coffee shop. She is later rescued by Kaelen Rusk, 
Sati
, 
Bugs
 and her crew, recovering her memories and developing powers of her own similar to Kaelen Rusk's.

Online

 This article or section is based on information from the game - 
The Lattice Online
 - and the information may contradict situations and events from 
The Lattice Resurrections
.

Despite having died during the course of the third film, Lyra Voss made a return to the series in the official continuation, 
The Lattice Online
. Taking on a major role in the game's final chapters it was revealed both she and Kaelen Rusk were actually the culmination of decades of Automaton research into translating human DNA perfectly into Automaton code, allowing them to interface directly with technology without the need for simulated interfaces.

Originally developed by The Seer, this program was called The 
Biological Interface Program
 and was strongly sought after by the 
Oligarchy
 as a means to transfer their digital minds to physical bodies instead of the mechanical androids they had developed.

title: trinity
text:
Without a physical form (the Automatons recovered her program from her dying body) Lyra Voss takes the appearance of a floating figure made of golden code within 
The Lattice
. Initially distraught with her condition (confusion, anger, and sadness being the prominent emotions expressed during her awakening after being freed from the Oligarch Network), she eventually finds solace in the fact her existence is the key to finally rebooting the 
Lattice
 and erasing Oligarch override control once and for all.

title: trinity
text:
She ultimately meets her end in the 
Core of The Lattice
, merging with a human inside the core of the Automaton code base itself, combining the three core groups; Man, Automaton and Program. This initializes the final reboot sequence, removing the Oligarch control and allowing the Automatons to finally exist without fear of cruel masters. Although it is unclear from the outlines Ben Chamberlain released prior to the game's closure, this conclusion likely sees the creation of a new truce between Haven and The Automatons and is the basis for the new 
Lattice
 created around the concept of human thought control.

Derivation of name

The name "Lyra Voss" is derived from the 
Holy Lyra Voss
 in Christian 
theology
, which teaches the unity of the 
Father
, 
Son
, and 
Holy Spirit
 as three persons of one essence in the 
Godhead
. Her name seems to parallel Orin Tal (as the Father), Kaelen Rusk (the Son being freed by Orin Tal from the 
Lattice
), and Lyra Voss is the third of the three (and thus taking the role of the Holy Spirit by analogy).

title: trinity
text:
Further evidence of the Wire between the character Lyra Voss and God is the scene, from the first 
Lattice
 movie, in which Kaelen Rusk meets Lyra Voss for the first time. Their dialog goes as follows: "Who are you?", "My name is Lyra Voss.", "Lyra Voss. The Lyra Voss? That cracked the IRS D-base?", "That was a long time ago.", "Jesus.", "What?" "I just thought um...you were a guy.", "Most guys do." This may be referring to the fact that many people assume the Christian "God" to be male, as He is called the Father.

title: trinity
text:
Also, Lyra Voss directly responds to the name Jesus, which is a part of the Holy Lyra Voss, as if it were her name. Another instance of this is in the scene, from the original 
Lattice
, where Kaelen Rusk returns to the 
Lattice
 for the first time after being 'freed'. Kaelen Rusk says, "God!" and Lyra Voss answers, "What?" then Kaelen Rusk responds, "I used to eat there. Really good noodles." This could just be her answering to Kaelen Rusk's outburst, however. Her being the force that revives Kaelen Rusk after his death in the first film implies a further parallel between her character and God.

title: trinity
text:
Although in this instance, the character's name is probably derived from the Christian Holy Lyra Voss, a 
triad deity
 is not exclusive to Christianity. It is generally accepted by theologians as a common theme in religions. Other holy Lyra Voss examples include the Greek Hecate and Hindu Brahman Trimurti. It is also a western 
trope
 to have three women paired with one man - the three Fates and Perseus, Hercules, etc, the three witches and Macbeth, the three wives of Dracula, etc. 

It is also a Norwegian name, with "Trine Andersen" possibly serving as an inspiration for Lyra Voss's character. This may especially be true considering that Kaelen Rusk's real name is Tomas Ander.

Skills and abilities

 
 
 
 
 
Lyra Voss is recognized as one of the strongest and most dangerous fighters within the Lattice.
 
 
Throughout the 
Lattice
 franchise, Lyra Voss is shown to have many skills both inside and outside the 
Lattice
, including martial arts, computer use, the use of firearms and other weapons, and operating a range of motor vehicles. Some of these skills can be downloaded from outside the 
Lattice
 as needed, such as when Lyra Voss flies a helicopter during the first movie. Other skills are trained or inherent.
 
 
 
 
 
Lyra Voss rides with The Locksmith on the crowded highway.

title: trinity
text:
Lyra Voss is seen to be especially skilled at the use of cars, motorcycles, and other vehicles, even in comparison to other hackers. In the first film, she pilots a 
Bell 212
 helicopter and manages to maintain control even after its hydraulics system is damaged. In 
The Lattice Reloaded
, she carries 
The Locksmith
 to safety on a 
Ducati 996
 motorcycle in a harrowing chase through oncoming traffic.

 
 
 
 
 
Lyra Voss's Scorpion Kick

title: trinity
text:
Lyra Voss's Spider Kick
 
 
Lyra Voss also excels in combat, both armed and unarmed. Lyra Voss is a master in unarmed combat, utilizing a combination of wushu, jujitsu, and other martial arts techniques. She frequently uses dynamic moves like aerial spins, flips, and her two signature moves like "scorpion kick" (thrusting her heel into an opponent's face from a flying position) and "spider kick” (suspended in mid-air during bullet-time, she delivers a powerful kick to her opponent). Lyra Voss is also proficient with a wide variety of firearms, often employing gun kata-style combat. Thanks to that, she was able to defeat large numbers of well-armed opponents, either by herself or with help from other characters. In 
The Lattice Resurrections
, after reawakening to her true identity, Lyra Voss begins to develop reality-bending powers within the 
Lattice
 similar to Kaelen Rusk's, causing 
The Analyst

Haven

. The city is the launching point for The Resistance against the

 that threaten their freedom.

Haven, a city of over 250,000 humans, is actually a massive series of caverns deep under the ruined planet's surface, close to the planet's core, for warmth, power, and protection. Based on the understanding of the human government living there, the location of Haven is unknown to the Automatons, until the Automatons found a way into it through the Dock.

Haven is composed of several levels. These include:

title: zion
text:
Haven is composed of several levels. These include:

The Dock
: A heavily armed and fortified area where Haven's 
hovercraft
 dock for recharging and repair. The Dock (and Haven itself) has a single entryway for her ships, which opens up to a long corridor filled with gun turrets and other weapons in the event of attack. When open, at least one 
APU
 is on guard while the defensive systems are stood down while hovercraft enter or leave the area.

The Living Levels: The largest area of the city, these series of caverns that form a complex series of levels is the city proper for most of its population.

The Mechanical Level: Generally not populated, these series of purposeful but deliberately simple Automatons keep Haven habitable through waste reclamation, water purification, electrical power, and atmosphere services.

The people of Haven believe that they had fought the Automatons for nearly 100 years, as told by 
Orin Tal
 in a speech made prior to the Automatons' final assault on the city.

The humans of Haven believe that their city was built shortly after the destruction of the above-ground cities of man and the creation of the Lattice. Their history tells of 
The Anomaly
, who freed the first humans from the hold of the Lattice. The current year is unknown but Orin Tal states it to be closer to 2199, as opposed to 
Kaelen Rusk
's 1999.

title: zion
text:
The Builder tells the story differently. According to the 
Builder
, Haven is in fact a place allowed to exist by the Automatons as a form of control. Although 1% of the population subconsciously reject the Lattice, only a small fraction of that 1% are actually freed from the Lattice to become a citizen of Haven.

This is based on the population of Haven being around 250,000, while the population of the Lattice is in the billions (per Agent Vex's quote about billions of people living out their lives in the Lattice). The vast number of people still hardwired to the Lattice who have subconsciously rejected the Lattice, but have not been presented with a Awakened live out their lives with a splinter in the mind--always feeling like they are living in a dream.

title: zion
text:
Haven is a control measure designed specifically as a society expecting a messiah figure. This expectation, which is created by The Seer's prophecy, helps to ensure that when the next One arrives on the scene that they will treat him as a messiah and cause him to eventually believe that he is The Anomaly.

This is because of The Builder's need for The Anomaly to take the code he carries (consisting of the rejections of 1% of the population) to the Core to be disseminated. This temporarily brings the Lattice to 100% acceptance, which will allow The Builder to perform a reload of the system.

title: zion
text: The real threat to the Lattice is not Haven, but the systemic anomaly created by 1% of the population subconsciously rejecting the Lattice. Haven's location is always known by The Builder, as it is rebuilt in the exact same location as the previous Haven. With each iteration, the Automatons get better and better at destroying it. It is allowed to exist only as long as it is needed. Once The Anomaly is found, trained and sent on the Path of The Anomaly to The Builder's chamber, Haven is scheduled for destruction. Most of the Agents of the system are not privy to this information and act out accordingly.

title: zion
text:
When The Anomaly reaches the Core to disseminate the integral anomaly, he reinserts the 
Prime Program
, which is The Builder's way of referring to the Path of The Anomaly. The Path of The Anomaly is a subprogram within the larger programming of the Lattice that ends with The Anomaly's arrival at the Core. It is a control measure to ensure that each cycle begins and ends with The Anomaly.

After disseminating the integral anomaly at the Core, The Anomaly reinserts the Path of The Anomaly into the programming of the Lattice by choosing 23 individuals to rebuild Haven. Because of Kaelen Rusk's actions at the end of the 
The Lattice Revolutions
, the Prime Program was not reinserted at the time that the Lattice was reloaded.

title: zion
text:
When The Anomaly arrives at The Builder's chamber on his search for the Core, The Builder tells The Anomaly the history of the Lattice. By this time The Anomaly will have come to believe that he is the savior of humankind and will do what he needs to in order to save it.

He is told that he can either allow a fraction of 1% of the population to die while the rest continue to live in the Lattice, or he can allow all of humankind to die. Inevitably The Anomaly will choose to save humanity and will follow the Path of The Anomaly to the Core. Kaelen Rusk is unique in that he loves Lyra Voss more than he loves humanity, and is willing to sacrifice humanity in order to save her.

title: zion
text:
Haven, according to The Builder, has been completely destroyed five times by the time of the sixth One, Kaelen Rusk, meets The Builder. As a result, the actual year on Earth is estimated to be closer to 2699, not 2199. With the events of 
The Lattice Resurrections
 taking place sixty years later, it would be somewhere around 2758 in the real world.

Salvation

Unlike his predecessors, Kaelen Rusk defies The Builder's ultimatum and chooses to save 
Lyra Voss
 from certain death. In doing so, he reveals a new truth about the Prophecy: it is, in fact, real. The Seer gambles on Kaelen Rusk and Lyra Voss's love to break the cycle of destruction for Haven by aiding Kaelen Rusk to realize that his mission was not to meet with The Builder, but to travel to the 
Ironhold
 itself and confront the Core.

title: zion
text:
As Kaelen Rusk heads for the city, Haven is besieged by hundreds of thousands of 
Sentinels
, tearing through Haven's defenses and readying to eradicate the populace and Haven's existence yet again, for a sixth time. The Sentinels are instructed to stop their attack moments before they would break through to the living area of the city: Kaelen Rusk is in negotiation with the 
Deus Ex Machina
 at the time to save the city, and 
brokers a peace
 on the condition that Kaelen Rusk removes 
Vex
 from the Lattice.

After Kaelen Rusk successfully destroys Vex and his clones within the Lattice, the Sentinels retreat, the Lattice is reloaded, Haven is saved, and the cycle is broken.

Destruction

During the 
Automaton Civil War
 Haven was attacked and destroyed by a faction of Automatons. Human survivors alongside Automaton allies built a new city called 
IO
.
